It's like Final Fantasy finally meets Tower Defense!
Defender’s Quest: Valley of the Forgotten is yet another tower defense game on the list. But surprisingly, this one comes together with a little twist attached to it. It’s an RPG Tower Defense Game! Yeah, you've heard it right. Someone actually combined both of those genres. Initially it may sound like an unlikely combination, but like salt and caramel, they've really complemented each other in surprising ways.
This game is a 2D game with a unique blend of Tower Defense and RPG created by Level Up Labs. Rather than having "towers", you have party members that you need to strategically place them around the map, of which purpose is to defend your main character Azra. Unlike a simple tower defense game, however, you can level up and equip items for your companions to help them improve in combat. A very nice combination indeed!
You take the role of Azra, a royal librarian of the Kingdom of Ash which is currently being ravaged by a unknown plague. Azra gets infected and thrown into 'The Pit', a place where all dead or dying are kept to maintain the kingdom safe from plague. Those who die from the plague become 'Revenants', undead monsters that are immune to physical harm. But Azra soon discovers that she has the power to enter both the living world and the 'Half-Way' world, a place between the living realm and the realm of the dead. In this realm, she can summon her companions to fight the Revenants in their spirit form and eventually beat the crap out of them.
There are around 30 levels to survive, but you'll lose more time than you think while playing them. You can actually go back and try to beat levels on harder difficulties. (The range starts from Casual, continues with Normal and Advanced but doesn't forget to include the Extreme difficulty.) Doing so, throws a tougher, more varied group of enemies at you that offers greater XP and loot to help you in your journey.
During battle you can change the attitude of your party members. You can tell them to favor boss monsters, to attack only the weak enemies, to use the more powerful skills on stronger enemies and so on. In addition, your companions have boost levels that you need to increase in order to give them access to their strongest skills. However, doing that you spend precious energy, called Psi in the game, every time you boost their abilities, which will sometimes force you to make tough decisions.
You're also given a tremendous amount of control when it comes to the game's speed. You can pause everything, while still being able to place units and upgrade them, or pump the speed all the way up to 4x if you're the impatient type of gamer. Defender's Quest is very respectful of the player in every number of aspects. Controls and hotkeys are configurable, cutscenes and conversations can be skipped and rewatched later if you choose so, and I'll tell you a secret. The rate at which experience is earned can also be increased from the options. The developers put a lot of love in their game as you can see. That being said, you can get to the end on normal difficulty in five hours or less. But personally, I've spent more than 14 hours going back and forward to complete perfect runs on every stage. There's plenty of optional content that will make up for your hard earned money.
Other than fighting through the story, at a certain point you will gain access to a list of challenge bonus battles (including two endless battles). These will offer you yet more experience as well as precious unique books to augment your main character fighting skills. Bonus battles will automatically be unlocked once you earn enough blue and yellow stars from fighting in normal battles.
Once you complete the normal game, you will unlock the New Game+. Which is the story written all over again, but at a much harder level, with even better rewards and the ability to upgrade all those unique items you've found during the normal game. The New Game+ will also have it's own bonus battle list.

Mafia II is another addition to the GTA/Godfather crime syndicate sandbox genre.
Pros: The main storyline is pretty well-written and the games does a good job of providing you with an authentic early-to-mid 20th century atmosphere as you move through various periods in the "mafia era". The gameplay works just about as well as you'd expect. The story is what makes the game.
Cons: For a sandbox game, there really isn't much to do outside the main storyline. The side-missions, upgrades and other activities in the game go remarkably unnoticed. That's a huge black mark on this game's record and puts well below other game series in the genre (Saints Row, GTA, Godfather, etc.). The mainstory line is about 15 hours long, which is short even for other sandbox games, and then the other stuff just isn't there. The storyline feels complete, but missing essential elements beyond the storyline which would have made it better. Also, there is a painfully large amount of driving with nothing else going on causing an already short game to feel stretched out.
Verdict: At full price, I wouldn't buy this game again, but this being Steam and all, you can pick up for cents on the dollar. The 15 hours of main storyline gameplay is fun and immersive and it's worth picking up at the right price, but if you are looking for a 40+ sandbox game, I reccommend you look for better titles in the genre because the only way you'll reach 40 hours is with 30 hours of driving.

I played this game like crazy when I was young. It's really hard until you get the hang of it, and then you become basically unstoppable. The most scary part of the game for me was level 7, the first time I encountered the first boss. I went out into this big lava room and the boss made such a horrible scary sound when he appeared, and it killed me. Then I would hide inside the tunnel leading to the bosses' room, and it would appear nearby. My heart would nearly stop when I would hear the sound effect he would make, because then I knew he was nearby. The boss would fire missles into my tunnel I was hiding in, and the little green balls would lock onto my ship and destroy me. After trying countless times to beat him by shooting at him from inside my not-so-safe tunnel, I made a bold and daring move. I left the tunnel. And amazingly, even though I played only with the keyboard, my little fingers would move so fast I could slide up, down, right, left and spin in all kinds of crazy circles, the little green balls would try to lock onto my ship but I was able to dodge them all. The funnest part of this game for me was its built-in replay recording feature, which will record a replay of your game. Once I got good at beating the boss, I increased the difficulty level to "insane", and recorded countless epic replays of me beating the boss on insane. He would shoot missles  as fast as a machine gun on insane difficulty, and every one of those missles would explode into a cloud of green balls. Hundreds of green balls would be in the air at once. Shoulda been impossible for me to dodge them all. Even just one or two of them hitting me would destroy my ship at that level of difficulty. But I would dodge them all. I would do loop to loops around the boss, zig-zagging through all the green balls, all the while shootting at him and throwing his own green balls right back at him, destroying him with his own green balls! It was so much fun. Some of those replays were so insane, I wish I still had the recordings, but that was a long time ago. This is one of the few games where you will often be turning both up/down plus turning right/left plus sliding up/down plus sliding right/left plus moving forward/backward plus shooting --- all at the same time!

-  Some of the environments are pretty.
- It's short, so you don't have to endure it for long.
The Bad:
-The level design later in the game is pretty awful.  I frequently found myself alternating between baby's-first-platformer and obtuse sections where I had no idea where I was supposed to go.
-The core mechanic is poorly executed.  It's difficult to gauge how far the rocket boots will take you, or how far a gapple will propel you.  I found myself very frustrated as I had to replay sections over and over again.
-The voice acting is lackluster.  It ranges from "Meh" for the protagonist and his daughter, to ear-grating for the character Maddie.  I think her voice actress was trying to hide an accent.
The Ugly:
-One of the worst stories in any game I've ever played.  You're never given any reason to care about this uncle, who ***SPOILER WARNING***

Resurrected as a vampire after your death, you are recruited to assist in an ongoing war of attrition between several vampire clans who vie for control of Los Angeles. Using a combination of stealth, cunning and brute force, only you can ultimately shape the result of the conflict.
Famously released in an unfinished state (though several patches and mods have been released that largely fix this), Bloodlines is a flawed yet absolutely captivating gem of a game that takes the stealth-action RPG hybrid gameplay of series such as Deus Ex and Thief, drapes it in a veneer of equal parts Anne Rice sensual horror and goth club sleaze, and ties it all together with an excellent script dripping with lore, mystery, sexuality, and violence. There's plenty of replay value to be had as well thanks to the diverse array of vampire clans one can play as; from the seductive Toreador or traditionalist Ventrue, to the monstrous Nosferatu or gibbering and insane Malkavian. Just be ready to do some patching after you've installed the game.

This is it. The quintessential vampire game. There are many reviews that highlight its pros and cons, so I will just say this: it's very good; play it. Be aware, however, that installing the unofficial patch isn't just recommended, but necessary, since the game is very buggy (which is by no means the developer's fault, but rather the publisher's). So check out the community hub for guides on how and where to get patches and various mods.
First timers should also be careful in choosing the clan for their inaugural playthrough. For instance, Malkavian are a... peculiar breed, and some of the dialogue may be a bit confusing; you might also hear voices and talk to objects. Nosferatu, on the other hand, have an altered physical appearance (more "monstruous"), so moving around and interacting with various NPCs can be a challenge; thankfully you can use sewers, and an innate cloaking ability. Even Ventrue can be difficult, because they are selective with their food; so you won't be able to feed off rats or homeless people. Awesome game that is essentially competitive multiplayer Terraria.
You choose between 3 classes (knight, archer, builder), but builder is the deepest and most fun addition to this kind of game. As a builder, you gather resources Terraria style (chopping trees, mining rocks) and use those resources to build various things ranging from walls and doors to workshops and work benches. The latter can increase the number of things you can build significantly. Building things like drills for faster harvesting, catapults and ballistas for siege weaponry, and powder kegs to wreck enemy defenses (and boy do they).
The tug of war combat is extremely fun, balanced, and fast paced, with matches lasting upwards of half an hour. You win by taking control of all spawning points and then defeating all enemy players. It's not a unique mode, but the gameplay around it is extremely addictive. You want to keep playing more matches because of how different each game feels.
I recommend this to the creative builder type that plays Terraria. Playing this only for the combat can get boring, but focusing on building is extremely fun and makes the work you do feel useful.
It can be a good game alone. But, it can be an amazing game if you have friends to play it with. It's pretty much focused on multiplayer so don't buy it for singleplayer.

LISA: a miserable journey and a fantastic game.
At a glance, you might confuse LISA with some typical modern indie expulsion of cargo-cult nostalgia, or think it's one's of gaming's many cringeworthily immature attempts to 'get dark'.
Don't. This game deserves your attention.
LISA's surreal, insightful 'man's world' takes you to bleak, scary places but keeps you truckin' on with sharp black humour and just enough dangerous hope. Consequences are explored cleverly; consequences of the strange apocalypse, of your own decisions, of plain old rotten luck. The audiovisual design and deft game-mechanical touches elegantly create moods; of alienation, doom and fleeting beauty.
This may sound over-the-top for an RPGmaker side-scroller, but it isn't. LISA is honestly one of the best games I've seen in years. I'm not going to spoil the story for you; just play it, you won't regret it.
~
Uppers: A creative, daring story in a well-realised setting that uses its dreamlike quality brilliantly. A wealth of fun characters to grieve for and misplace. Catchy music. Thought-provoking situations. Surprisingly fun combat. Genuine humour and understanding of the human condition. Replay value that'll bring you right back like a kicked dog. Flashes of virtue and hope that only hurt you more.
~
Downers: Quite laggy in some areas which may necessitate a quick game restart. I think there's one very minor mechanical limitation that won't bother you if you don't notice it, so I won't reveal it. I permanently lost Terry early on and now I can't stop crying.
~
The Bottom Line: LISA grabs your mind and bites down hard. This game puts much more expensive developments to shame in its intelligence, thoughtfulness and sheer fun factor. Do yourself a favour and give it a go.

8/10 - TL;DR - Great story, emphasis on choices...but felt a little railroaded.  Excellent gameplay.  Excellent artwork.  Excellent soundtrack.
Story:
(MINOR SPOILERS)
This was a very artfully executed RPG with a masterfully told story.  The opening alone is one of the strongest openings I've seen from a game in a long time.  The main characters had interesting backstories which I felt compelled to figure out.  I've not had a game make me feel as much as this one did in such a short period of time.  All that being said, I felt a bit railroaded in my playthrough.  I was forced to make horrible decisions (which is fine), but I didn't feel that what I chose affected the story very much.  I remained very much an anti-hero though I did my very best to play the "white knight."  Not the worst thing in the world, but that's where I think there could've been some improvement.
Gameplay:
The battle system is reminiscent of Earthbound.  It is turn-based and filled to brim with interesting status effects and skills.  The combo system used by the main character (and a spattering of others) was very visceral and felt quite fulfilling.  I was also impressed by the massive roster of pickable characters to choose from.  Finally, one of the coolest elements of the game is the overworld exploration.  Lots of traditional pixel-based RPGs are viewed top-down, but this one is a sidescroller with platforming elements.  It made for engaging exploration.
Artwork:
The art of this game was what drew me in initially.  Most old-school RPGs go with the traditional JRPG/anime theme, but Lisa stands apart with its gruff biker-types and washed-up middle-aged drug addicts.  The art isn't beautiful.  It's quite ugly...in the best way possible.  If you're looking for a game that ventures off the beaten path in terms of artwork, I highly recommend Lisa.
Music:
Lisa had one of the most bizarre soundtracks I've ever heard from a game.  That being said, I loved it.  Widdly 2 Diddly managed to add wonderful atmosphere to a very unusual game.  It even played off of old RPG tropes (success music sounding less than successful) that managed to make me laugh from time to time.  And when the music wasn't making me laugh, it was making me feel more intensely the painful moments of my protagonist.  Excellent soundtrack.

So this popped up yesterday on my Wishlist as a Sale item for £7ish, being a huge Cricket fan as well as Cricket Groundsman I just had to bite the bullet and grab it regardless of the lack of activity and Mixed reviews (most of them said if you already own CC2015 then it's not worth it but if not then try it).
It's simple in design, no where near as detailed as the FM series or Motorsport Manager, getting into the first game is quick & easy after a few minutes of Menu Hopping. But what it lacks in prettiness it gives bundles back in Statistics on each and every player (a Cricket fans Dream), there's a ton of leagues to play with and all formats of the game are covered including the chance to Captain/Manage National Teams.

There's Training Options for your players, you can Buy & Release Players at the start of each Season, it's pretty much all the basics of Football Manager without the highly over-detailed additional areas.
My favourite area is the 'Pitch Groundsman' where you can determine the style of Wicket to be played on for your next home game...like we do that in the real world...!
I've already found some pretty obvious bugs (last update was in January with no sign of the Devs/update since) which are slightly annoying but nothing game breaking as of yet.
I'm gonna keep it and see how it goes as it's not that bad it needs a refund, it was only a couple of Pints worth and it's something to while away the hours at work on Match & Rainy Days or when the Wifes watching Celebrity Big Bloody Brother! If you like Cricket get it and give it a go and see for yourself, it's cheap.

As expected, CC16 is exactly the same as year before and before that, with nothing but an update to the player database - though even that feels poorly researched. To ask £15-20 for what amounts to a patch to a previous game feels disingenuous to this series' fans. Even months before 2017 is released, the game only reduces to £9.99.
As someone who has played since CC05, I have noted with a great deal of disappointment how little these games have moved on from year to year. The developers look to quantity (adding new competitions and teams) rather quality (creating a discreeter game with more longevity), and in doing so ignore much of the feedback from their fans - who offer such in goodwill and hope that the next year will be the year Cricket Captain finally pulls itself together.
Each year we are promised a better engine that will offer more realistic scenarios, especially in one day and T20 modes, but this has never really come to fruition. Rather, one day games become steadily harder and more tedious to play and T20 is often unplayable. Instead of a better game we are given "better" graphics in highlights - which most people skip - though the differene from edition to edition is so minimal.
While we all understand that this game is developed by a small team, Childish Things are wasting a lot of goodwill that their fans are granting them. Rather than taking two years to genuinely overhaul the game and create an enjoyable and diverse experience - which no one would truly complain about - they throw out the same thing over and over, year after year and are verging on taking advantage of their fans.
A major problem is the lack of competition. But for Cricket Coach, Cricket Captain hasn't seen any competition for years and as such knows that cricket fans, especially those that wish for a management style game, will have no choice but to buy their products. As such a long time consumer, it is so disappointing to see what could be an excellent and innovative series fall to laziness.

Overall, I've had an exciting time outrunning enemy corvetts and sinking pirate frigates, taking their flags and using them to patch my sails.
Currently, I play a corvett decked to the nines, a pretty skilled captain, and a pet wookie named Steve.
The game's progression is a good pace for me and you'll hardly ever run out of things to do. Currently, i'm trying to find a poorly defended port so I can capture a man-o'-war or something.
With that, and the consideration the game is free, I have no issues with recomending this if you have some extra time on your hands. It's fun, decently paced, and it'll give you a few good stories to tell.

Mafia II is another addition to the GTA/Godfather crime syndicate sandbox genre.
Pros: The main storyline is pretty well-written and the games does a good job of providing you with an authentic early-to-mid 20th century atmosphere as you move through various periods in the "mafia era". The gameplay works just about as well as you'd expect. The story is what makes the game.
Cons: For a sandbox game, there really isn't much to do outside the main storyline. The side-missions, upgrades and other activities in the game go remarkably unnoticed. That's a huge black mark on this game's record and puts well below other game series in the genre (Saints Row, GTA, Godfather, etc.). The mainstory line is about 15 hours long, which is short even for other sandbox games, and then the other stuff just isn't there. The storyline feels complete, but missing essential elements beyond the storyline which would have made it better. Also, there is a painfully large amount of driving with nothing else going on causing an already short game to feel stretched out.
Verdict: At full price, I wouldn't buy this game again, but this being Steam and all, you can pick up for cents on the dollar. The 15 hours of main storyline gameplay is fun and immersive and it's worth picking up at the right price, but if you are looking for a 40+ sandbox game, I reccommend you look for better titles in the genre because the only way you'll reach 40 hours is with 30 hours of driving.

Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten is an RPG/Tower Defense hybrid. At first, wasn't sure how well the genres would mix. Now, I can say they mix well, at least for this game. It reminds me a lot of Shining Force meets tower defense with realtime combat. The storyline is great, and not overbearing. I enjoyed reading the cutscenes quite a bit. Good sense of humor put into the game as well. I have not beat it yet, so this is based on what I have seen a few hours in.
Positives
- Great writing/story. Enough character development to understand the story and the role you play in it. At the same time, not necessary if you just want to skip to the tower defense part (though it is worth reading, I assure you).
- Decent variety of tower/class types to choose from. You can choose if you want to specialize in a particular type of defender rather than being forced to use them all. Like most tower defense games, you will want some variety though.
- Many quality of life features such as individual settings to save for each defender, prompts asking if you want to place defenders in the same place as last time when repeating a map, quick sell options when upgrading equipment, dialogue skip buttons, and many more. The developers were very considerate of our time to include efficient options.
- Good replay value. Can go back to the maps you have done before to grind or to try a more challenging version for better rewards.
- Well composed music. The music assets are very fitting and relaxing. A great addition to an already entertaining game.
- Very robust controls. Clear usable keyboard shortcuts for almost all functions. Many different time controls to slow down or speed up combat to a pace you are comfortable with. And of course, with the ability to pause.
- Permanent gear and skill upgrades for the defenders. As opposed to many tower defense games, there are progression elements that will stick with your defenders between maps. Buying/earning better weapons that will stay with your defender until you upgrade helps this feel more RPGish. Skills can be retrained for a reasonable cost of in game coin.
Negatives (To be honest, there are not many negative points for this game in my opinion)
- Lacking in character customization. While I realize the game is telling a story, I would have liked the ability to choose the gender of the main character. Perhaps if the campaign is completed, there will be something after that for the end game. Not sure.
- On the matter of customization, I would have liked to do more than just change the colors of the defenders. Hair styles, a few different faces, nothing major.
- Not enough variety in character drawings. This one is a bit nit-picky, but I am struggling to find complaints :p The only time you really see the character drawings in a form that matters is in the cutscenes. The problem with that is the same stances and reaction drawings are recycled throughout the game. I would have liked to see a bit more unique drawings for varying situations.
- While the music is a great asset to the game, it does not repeat or transition cleanly in some cases.
- Some of the skill progressions at low level seem a little lackluster. For example, a 2% chance to bleed targets per hit feels a bit useless when many of these things die relatively quick. I would prefer either high chance or guaranteed trigger with low or weakened effects to balance it. Granted, I am sure these abilities work well on bosses and larger enemies.
TL;DR
A great game with a mix of RPG and Tower Defense elements. Excellent musical scores, and a good storyline to boot. Well worth picking up at full price or on sale. I highly recommend this game.

(Purchased through a Humble Bundle for a small amount of list price)
I got this game to play local co-op, so I can't say much about the online multiplayer as far as how matchmaking is.
Here's the rundown:
This is a pretty straightforward top-down dual-stick shooter, where you and your team of up to four Helldivers have to complete all of the objectives in the procedurally generated map to complete the mission.
There are a couple dozen weapons and at least 25 different "strategems" (which are little items or attacks you can call in, like ammo, an airstrike, or a vehicle) to choose from, each having its own feel and use, and each being upgradable.
A large amount of weapons and outfits are only available as DLC, so just know that there is more content to purchase if you want to.
You can easily kill your teammates by accident, and you will. A lot.
Every set of levels is a planet you conquer, which, when completed, earns you a new item.
This is a pretty fun game, and an awesome one to play with friends.
Pick it up on sale with your friends.

HELLDIVERS is a top down shooter. It has been meant for the PS4 but then came on PC.
Set in a future where earth is a big alliance, under control of a managed democracy, this game already promises well. So let's see the
PROS
+Great backstory. I won't spoil it to you.
+Intuitive controls, and original support call system: You can call for resupplies and fire support using a peculiar key combination system, like cheats in GTA.
+Well-made weapons: There are quite a few weapons, and they all have their pros and cons, sometimes you are forced to change weapons because your current weapon isn't suited for the mission.
+Teamwork. A lot of it. The game offers quite a few ways to put your team to good use. From choosing complementary equipment, tanks, and assist-reloading heavy weapons, teammates are invaluable. Best played with 3 friends.
+Unforgiving friendly fire: Yep. There's friendly fire. And a lot of it. Your teammates are squishy, and so are you. See that giant heavy caliber rifle in your hands? It oneshots enemies. And so does to teammates.
+Good unlock and progression system.
+Democracy is life
But, not everything is good in HELLDIVERS. There are a few
CONS
-Too many DLCs. I get that the devs need money, but there are way too many, and adding stuff that is REQUIRED in some cases. Plus, the DLC equipment is all available from start and is not to be unlocked.
-A few bugs. There are few of them, but this few can easily be gamebreaking. Although rare, a bug could end your mission.
-Stealth could've been better: Having a suppressed weapon won't change anything, you can't go stealth.
--Verdict--
HELLDIVERS is a nice game, and strangely doesn't suffer from the port from console to PC. It will deliver a lot of fun with friends, and it will make you swear a lot. The pricetag is quite high and difficult to justify, because of the so many DLCs and the age of the game. If you want to buy, i suggest you get the digital deluxe to fully enjoy it, and buy it from external sites at a lessened price.

After 508.2 hours of gameplay, I can say that this game can be broken down as such:
The Good:
- Gameplay is smooth, fun, stressful and sometimes very nailbiting or hairpulling.
- If you can get into story made in every encounter, you'd have more stories then R.L Stine working with H.P Lovecraft on a great acid trip.
- The soundtack is so fitting, and really seals the deal.
- An adundence of content. Ships, weapons, play styles.
- Questlines and quests make getting the full experience without being the best possible!
The Bad:
- The as first said, the gameplay can be nailbiting, or hairpulling. OFTEN. You will lose; a lot. Your people will die; a lot.  You may even cry.
- RNG (Random Number Generator) is a pretty heavy factor. (Ex. Help Mantis or Turn Him In?)
- MAKE SURE YOU READ - There are sequences that require you to have read the beacon entry box.
- You do need to micro-manage a lot. Fuel, Rockets, Drone Parts, Weapons, Crew Members, Augements, and even at some points you enemies.
- The final boss will end your happiness a lot more than once.
With all this being taken into account, and the fact that I have NEVER BEATEN THE FINAL BOSS: Get this game.
Why?
Because its a great game, that will have you coming back for more; no matter how much it hits you then sends you into your room, you will come back. You will want to get all the ships, try all the weapons, kill all the pirates, see all the races, et cetera. Not to mention, the ratio of money paid to hours of content would put most Triple A titles to shame (AND THIS GAME DOESNT EVEN HAVE MULTIPLAYER)

This is one of those games I find immensely frustrating to play, but also highly addictive. I am a huge cricket fan, and the truth is there is no alternative out there for in-depth, strategy or management games for the sport. If you're a fan and want to give it a spin then go for it, but wait for a sale and get it at a low price, because despite the experience and longevity of the franchise the game is bare-bones.
I would love to reach out to the developers and implore them to make changes for the next iteration, as the base game is enjoyable but in drastic need of more creative input! All we've seen in terms of additions in recent years has been the inclusion of new leagues. This is fine, but although diversifying the gameplay, does little to improve the experience.
None of these appear hard to implement, as other sport management sims have been doing it for decades, but could we please look to include...
1) an actual career mode, where you can change teams, move up the 'ladder' and perhaps take jobs in different countries.
2) some kind of basic player 'stats' system, so I can actually tell if my player is talented, notably with youth players, whose potential seems entirely arbitrary.
3) the ability to hire coaches, or a far more transparent coaching system that allows you to know how and when your players are improving.
These additions really are important for giving a player a sense that they are part of a management structure that is affecting the game world. They appear fairly minor changes that for me would make this game far easier to recommend, and would guarantee repeat custom.

I will say this upfront: if you are a hardcore Cricket fan, and if you enjoy the statistical side to the game, then you may end up liking this game. There are two core aspects to the game: selection of your team, and then setting fields and managing how aggressive your bowlers and batsmen are during the games themselves. You don’t have any direct control over the players, so in many ways it’s sort of a cricket match simulator. The amount of input you put into the game is quite minimal, so it feels like a casual game with a strong statistical emphasis. The main difficulty with the game is the selection process, as you don’t have access to any attributes, aside from their statistical records in previous matches, which like a real cricket selector means you either have to choose based on gut instinct, or record over a period of time.
Whilst this simplistic style of game can be endearing, ultimately it’s hard to recommend at this price, as the game has not fundamentally changed in over 15 years, and the incremental changes are hardly revolutionary. The graphics and UI are awful. The lack of a player editor to fix basic errors in details and ability means that to seasoned cricket fans the database will frustrate, as the game outside of England is not well scouted or balanced and don’t often reflect real world abilities. I understand the decision not to include editor is because the game is so similar to previous editions; fans would be able to update them themselves and wouldn’t spend the money. However, when the database is so fundamentally flawed, I cannot let it slide.
If you haven’t played this series before, it’s well worth a look. If you have a recent edition, there’s not enough new content to warrant the asking price.

This has quickly turned into one of the most creative games I've played in years.  It's a clever mix of comedy and grimdark.  Imagine if Earthbound took after the stylings of The Road.
The game is called 'The Painful RPG' for good reason.  There are many times where the game will be outright unfair to you in order to make your journey miserable.  It works for this game though, the pain it brings rarely halts your progress, but fits in perfectly with this twisted world.  You will be forced to make some choices you really won't want to make, and getting through this game without sacrifice is nearly impossible.  Some side advice, when given the choice, do not choose to play in Pain mode unless you know you are ready for what that entails.
If the trailer interests you at all, give this game a try.  If you are looking for something different, and don't mind playing a game that probably hates you, this game will suck you in like few others can, and stick with you looooong after you finish playing.

LISA is what you get if you crossed Fist of the North Star, Y: The Last Man, and Earthbound in a blender, threw in a heap of drugs on top and then pressed puree. Its a game that alternates between genuinely funny dark humor and soul crushing sadness. While I think a few  parts border on try-hard overall it does a good job maintaining that humanity a good bleak story needs in order to not be dumb nihilism. The game's atmosphere is quite unique, there's a lot of goofy weirdness going on but there's far darker things lying beneath the surface.
The gameplay is like Dragon Quest/Earthbound though its similar to Mega Ten in that status effects and debuffs are essential. The combat requires you to play smart, but its not really too difficult if you know your way around JRPGs. It does has some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t mechanics just to be cheap rather than hard though, such as instant kill moves that actually kill your characters (Though strangely enough I didn't run into this at all, this might have been patched) and other RNG things (Always save before resting aside from a few exceptions.) You also have to make choices that do impact the gameplay, but they're not game-ending if you know what you're doing. but they do matter and some decisions can you lock out on stuff.
Overall LISA stands among the best RPG Maker games and is a memorable RPG in its own right. Definitely play it if you're interested.

In a world where games are evolving in months rather than years it can sometimes be refreshing for game devs to stay true to a tried and tested formula.  In this case it isn't.
Maybe I'm a sucker for punishment, but I've owned 5 versions of this game since my original purchase of International Cricket Captain 2 and of all, the original was the best.
Over the years the 3d animations have slighly improved and there has been the introduction of things like Hawkeye.  But when year after year there is no improvement in the stroke animations making sense in terms of the line or length of the delivery, catches literally impossible for a human are regularaly taken, Hawkeye animations regularly don't match the delivery animation, and the aggression of the batting bears no resemblance to that chosen, eventually the charm wears away.
If you're after a cricket sim, this is your only option.
If you're after a cricket sim that evolves and improves between years, maybe a 20 year gap between purchases of this game is the only option.

2013 Game of the Year, hands down.
With apologies to Risk of Rain - it was pretty close.
King Arthur's Gold is just absolutely wonderful. From the lovely chiptune music to the diversity of the classes, to the way the map transforms over time and eventually collapses into the ocean, it's an almost perfect red vs blue game and one of the best retro games I've ever played.
There are only three classes, but what's so nice about them is they vary in playstyle, skill ceiling, and complexity. This is a game good and bad players can enjoy together. It's a game kids and adults can play against each other.
The knight is essentially pick up & play, very easy to learn and difficult to cause problems for teammates while learning. The archer is a bit more advanced but allows for players still getting their bearings (or who just aren't very good) to stay reliably out of harm's way while still contributing to the team objective.
For the advanced player, the builder has a complex range of tools, materials, and duties which are the meat & potatoes of this game, because it's the builder who makes the fortifications and defenses, designs the traps, determines the base layout, and is crucial to the infiltration of the enemy base. There is also resource management to consider here.
All of this stuff can lead to long contests, and in fact the map can become so wrecked that there's a "map ruined" option under the vote menu. This slow destruction of the level is more fun than it may sound. If one side decides to hold out and refuses the reset vote, you'll see pitched battles underwater, hunts in the collapsing and flooding tunnel systems, and probably more drowning than you'll encounter in all your other games combined.
The end result of all this delicious chaos is a rambling, relaxing mashup of Fat Princess, Ace of Spades, Worms, Terraria; and of course the great forgotten SNES classic King Arthur's World, from which KAG took much of its inspiration.
I cannot lavish enough praise on this game. There's even a solid co-op zombie mod if you haven't tired of zombies yet, complete with deep base building and boss portals to destroy. It's a surprisingly slow-paced and often suspenseful take on the genre, the likes of which we haven't seen since Urban Dead. Certainly not for everyone, but worth mention.
The rest of this game though -
for everyone. Nobody should be without KAG. It's as good as multiplayer gets.

I like the concept. It's an 80's style "Open world" game, so to speak. It's one of those VVVVVVV-type games. Very frustrating at times, but very rewarding when you get past a hard part and you unlock a new item. The items that you get along the way make some of the parts that you found hard at the beginning of the game easier, and some areas in the beginning are downright inaccesible until you get the items that allow you to get there. For example, there are one or two jumps at the beginning of the game that aren't possible without finding the double-jumping shoes. Of course, these items make the beginning stages easier, but then the game throws areas at you that are very difficult, even with the items. Keep in mind that this is a puzzle game, so you're not going to get too far if you just run into a room, throwing your life away. The game requires that you stop, access the situation, and find a quick and effective way to pass the area.
This game may be quite rage-inducing, but it's not one of those games that are deliberately made to be unfair. There may be a few annoying things here and there, though. For example, there is one room that is extremely difficult. If you pass the room, you can advance, but a couple of rooms later, you will find a room called "You better not go left" or something like that. Well, don't let your curiosity get the best of you. Going left in that room sends you back to the really hard room that you just passed.
As far as graphics and sound go, they're not terrible. Since the game is deliberately made to mimic the old-school arcade graphics and sound, you can't really say that they are poor. The game is easy to look at, but it's a little bland. The constant color scheme of grey, blue, black, and red, and occasionally one other color, can get a little boring to look at. The music? Well, there is none, but there are  plenty of perky, cheerful sound effects that are amusing to hear.
Overall, I think this game is very well done. It is kind of a short game, but the insane difficulty in the later areas of the game make the game seem longer. Also, being free, you don't have to worry about wasting money if it turns out that the game didn't impress you. This game at times punishes the curious. Having constant forks in the road makes the gameplay a little bit more branched out and open, as you have to make choices to either go where you were intending on going, or check out this other room that you found on the way, but sometimes, these rooms can send you back to where you were coming from, take you to a whole new area, send you down a huge hole that you have to get out of, and other undesireable things. I'd say, if you want to get far in this game, don't take detours. Get to where you want to go, and THEN you can explore a bit. This game does an exellent job of simulating that 80's arcade- style gameplay, and it's a definate recommendation to those that love that nostalgic feeling of playing old-school games.
Overall Rating: 8.5/10

Very fun multiplayer top-down shooter. This game requires you to work as a team against the aggressive enemies that are tying to prevent you from achieving your various goals, which change from mission to mission (they are varied enough to keep things interesting through many hours of gameplay). Level up to earn improved weapons and "strategems" - adiitional weapons, gear, static defense, air strikes, or vehicles - that you can call down from the skies via a varying-complexity button-press series. The tone of the game callls to mind the movie Starship Troopers, with the same satirical way of depicting a society based on waging war against other intergalactic races. Highly recommended for those who want to have fun working together to mow down enemies and keep the galaxy safe for democracy.

Progression is slow, rewards are uninteresting (although this is subjective), levels are repetitive and empty and the missions are always the same. The controls are also clunky (You can't quickly turn around, you can't shoot while prone and you can't snap aim which is often the cause of friendly fire because you'll start shooting the enemy who is attacking your friend while your helldiver is still leisurely sweeping over said friend) in addition to forcing every player to see the same screen meaning that if you go down and your teammates run away you can't see yourself.
When asked the developers say these design choices are made to make it more difficult. If this game becomes fun and engaging at some point then I didn't make it there, but I can't sleep at night because I keep wondering how this game got such high grades.
It's not the worst game ever though. The humor is good, shooting up the enemies feels satisfying, I've had no connectivity issues at all and the airdrop system is genuinly fun.
I wouldn't recommend it but if you're going to buy it, buy it while it's on sale. Honestly though, you should play alien swarm: reactive drop instead.

LISA is a terrible game. LISA, The Painful RPG, goes to many places many RPGs don't dare to go, for better or for worse. LISA can and most likely will punch your face in, only to step on your heart while you are down and make you laugh about it.
Because of that, it's probably one of the best games I've played in quite a while. Warning, TL;DR up ahead.
LISA, The Painful RPG, is an RPGMaker game set in the land of Olathe, Somewhere, USA. You take the pivotal role of Brad Armstrong, a balding drug addict hooked on Booze and Joy to take away the pain of a horrendous family life and god knows how many other regrets. Your sole goal is to find who is possible the last woman on the planet, a girl named Buddy who you helped raised from a baby. On your way, you'll face the worst humanity has to offer, and a few more other monstrosities along the way.
The actual RPG mechanics of the game, for an RPGMaker game, are solid, if not a bit unbalanced. Most of the stats are what they say on the tin, but some of the status ailments, if you forget what they do, offer no hints to what they actually accomplish. The combination of Fire and Oil is also hilariously OP, but in a world as fatal as LISA, is it that OP if it helps you keep people alive? Who could beat some of the more powerful bosses without Birdie around to spit oil and RT or Mad Dog to roast the competition? The combat itself is fairly gratifying, but out of all of the things LISA does, it might be the one thing it doesn't do perfectly. Almost as if there is stuff missing, like rock and paper missing scissors.
What isn't missing, however, is the on point music and sound design. The game can be fairly loud at times, but it is all in the grand scheme with the quirky and appropriate musical compositions W2D put together. It's honestly, in my opinion, one of the things LISA doesn't get enough credit for. The music sets a wonderful tone that follows your story superbly well, and even better when the music is yanked away. There is nothing more eerie than completing your goal, and being greated by a haunting tone of nothing but your footsteps. This design really does accentuate the real positive of LISA; the brilliant story.
LISA's story is a story that I can't help but appreciate. The main character, Bard Armstrong, proves to be such a character deserving of such empathy, but as the story goes along, both he and you are tested in how much you can take. People will die. Sometimes it's the people that you care the most about. Death, doubt, and betrayal are all around you, biting at your heels the moment you think you are in the clear, and there is never a moment where you are safe from the cruelty of post apocolyptic Olathe. The joking, dirty crust of LISA only lures you into the rotten, depressing core that will make you question what you do, and make you ponder the answers of questions you hope to never want to answer in the real world. It'll make you regret. It'll make you doubt. It'll make you hurt.
Even if you are squeamish, or not into RPGs, or any other excuse you could think of, reasonable or otherwise, I
you to take the risk and try LISA. It's a nasty, perverted, and disturbing game, but it is one of the best, if not
best RPG I've ever played. When LISA The Joyful comes out, buy that too. ♥♥♥♥, play LISA the First too. Absorb all the LISA you can get. Embrace it. Taste it. Digest it all. You won't regret it.

A tale of a broken man in a land of perverts and Joy.
Crude,Rude, and lewd. Lisa stars a man who's been broken for many years, incapable of forgiven himself for the loss of his sister long ago, both beaten and abused by their father. Brad Armstrong grew up protecting his friends and teaching karate in his dojo. Envied by his friends, hated by his father and deeply traumatized by the loss of his sister Lisa Armstrong he soon resorted to painkillers to forget and wipe away his regrets.
The world erased in a white flash, everything changed and everything destroyed. Mankind had its females seemingly removed from existance and the world crumbled into a inhospitable place, mutants, gangs, perverts, murderers and psychopaths rule the world now. In the middle of this is Brad who'd become addicted to Joy a new drug in this destroyed world now using it to kill his past. One day when taking a hit of Joy a baby all of a sudden appears in his arms, not only that but a female one.
Brad taking this child to his friends rejects the idea of giving her up for a better living to the local gang leader Rando, Instead he sees this child, now named Buddy as a secound chance. As his daughter or maybe just a means to put his past to rest. Wether its either is up to the player since not all of the cards are on the table.
The only thing known is that you will suffer and your actions will cause suffering.
All in all Lisa is a strong RPG, the roster is amazing, the story is blank enough to allow speculation.
The soundtrack is unique and amazing. The art style is off the walls and the whole world is a perverted joke and will have you cringing and creeped out by its warpedness. The game is a clear shoutout to Mother and Earthbound and Mad Max so old school gamers and RPG lovers with adore this game.
However due to its limited side scrolling the map can be confusing at times, cliffs can easily be jumped off of to your death, bugs and glitches do occur, enemies can permanantly kill allies and the amount of status effects can be confusing.
Its probably one of my most favorite games on steam right now and in existance, The story made me feel for Brad and Buddy aswell as making me feel the weight of losing an arm or a party member to one bad move or choice on my part. You will feel hurt playing this but in the end the game does what it wanted to, to make you feel.
Honestly whats a good game? One that makes you feel for what its created. Wether you on purposely play as a selfesh person or a selfless one, or something in between you will feel like you made a impact in this broken and beautifull world.

I've never written a single review for a video game on Steam but this one is so good I might as well write something.
I really like this game and if you are reading this you should definitly buy it.  But people like to see pros and cons so I might as well put them.
(TL;DR at the bottom)
Pros:
-Feels like Earthbound (always a good thing.)
-Soundtrack is amazing. It's psychadelic, creepy, and catchy.
-Combat is really cool and is very unique from many RPG games.
-This game is weird as ♥♥♥♥ but it's so original and different that it really stands out among indie games today.
-It's filled with secrets and extra content.
-There's a number of different paths to take that can change the future of how you play.
-It's ♥♥♥♥ing hilarious. This game is so random and weird and I'm always laughing at the many strange things I encounter.
-Art style is like Earthbound and it's crisp yet retro look is really appealing.
-It's mysterious and it hooks you in immediately. A lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥isn't (or hasn't yet been) explained and personally I like that.
Cons:
-Not for the faint of heart. This game isn't easy.
-You have to interact with everything. Sometimes one conversation with one NPC will dictate whether you will win a battle three hours later.
-It's a damn long game. I've played for four hours and though I'm not horrible at games, I still haven't finished it.
-It can frustrate the hell out of you sometimes.
-A LOT of backtracking. (But a certain item eventually can make that easier.)
-Choices. A lot of times you will be given catch 22 choices. Either way you're probably ♥♥♥♥ed and you have to decide which one you will be able to deal with better.
-It's pretty depressing honestly. The game is just really melancholy as even at times when you feel rewarded. You feel the pain of the characters in the game.
TL;DR
Buy it if you're down for something new and weird that feels like Earthbound. Or just want to play a really awesome RPG.

The italian beginning? Boring as hell. But the second/REAL introduction? Fantastic in how it creates an enviroment worth caring about instead of just making a level because the producers were like:
"Did you make the first level action packed?"
"No, we made it a returning of home intro, where the character slowly walks around the alleyways of his childhood homecity, seeing the crime and decay he will eventually become-"
"Does he have a shooting tutorial?"
"...No."
"Make the first level set in Italy. He can shoot germans and italian troops in it, it will be obvious in how he gains such prowess with a machine gun and fighting and stuff."
I know that isn't fair to the game designers or producers, but...even during the time I was playing this, it felt so empty in what I could actually do and what is there. In one mission, I am given the task of moving boxes for 10 dollars. I was so happy. Am I actually given the choice of being a honest man? But no, Only about a third of the way through he stops actually doing it and says "**** THIS NONSENSE, THIS IS HARDWORK" And goes on to punch and beat up poor workers who are doing the exact same thing he was doing earlier.
This creates a bad character, a bad motivation, and a horrible scenario. Vito shows no remorse for threatening these people who not only worked with his father but also are probably in the same situations as his deceased father, but who are also doing the work he refuses to do. The motivation for the player to do this instead of actually working is because you are trying to pay off a debt for this guy who...is actually a bit of a ♥♥♥♥♥, since Vito can beat up anyone who comes to his family and has a friend who should be willing to pay off this debt rather easily. And since we have a character who is unlikable and rather dumb and are suppose to relate to, the player feels like the game is telling us that we are dumb and desire to beat up people because we are foolish to see the opportunities in front of us.
I got an idea. Why doesn't Vito at first resist the mafia? Beat down mobsters who come after his family and the friends of his family, he and his friend Joe Pesci( DID IT AGAIN) start their own protection racket, and soon become the things they hate? That will create a motivation for the character to work for. But no, we gotta have a dramatic story about how crime doesn't pay...even though every single crime story to date is about that, and this doesn't do anything about it.
DO I RECOMMEND THIS GAME: NO

If there is a better RTS game currently on the market, I have yet to play it.
Since I played Company of Heroes 1, it was love at first sight. This sequel had a somewhat bumpy road immediately after its 2013 release (more on that later), but after three years of continuous patches and additional content from the developer, Company of Heroes 2 is a better game than its predecessor and, in my opinion, the finest strategy game ever made by Relic.
The reasons why playing Company of Heroes 2 is different than your regular run-of-the-mill RTS are twofold: gameplay mechanics and the atmosphere.
The gameplay is nothing like regular RTS "amass units, bigger mass wins" shtick.
Advanced mechanics such as cover system, suppression, and weapon penetration / armour thickness actually reward flanking and positional play. Infantry and heavy weapons are requisitioned as squads, which makes control much easier. You start with a few infantry squads, vie for control of the map. As the match progresses, vehicles, tanks and heavy artillery begin arriving on the field. Success or failure in skirmishes depends on not just on unit strengths and weaknesses, but also positioning and use of cover.
Mortars, machine guns and antitank guns are devastating but have a limited cone and must be positioned in advance. A single cheap machine gun can suppress and pin many infantry squads if attacked frontally, but will go down very fast if flanked. Mines can be placed that can completely turn the tide of the game - but a smart player will keep engineers close that can detect and disable minefields. You can tailor the terrain to your liking - set up sandbags, bunkers, firing positions, weld tank traps or wire off sections of the battlefield.
The game rewards mixed unit composition, using combined arms, and promotes sensible tactics for the era depicted. Bunching up your infantry is a surefire way to get them all suppressed, or maybe killed by indirect fire. Spreading your units out, using cover, and fixing and flanking enemy positions yields much better results. Resources are another thing brilliantly implemented. Resource income is tied to territory control - by capturing and holding territory points, you get a trickle of ammunition and fuel, which you can use to upgrade or build advanced units, respectively. This approach encourages spreading your troops all over the map, fighting for presence, instead of camping on one spot.
None of the above things are precisely NEW to strategy games on their own, but take all these things combined and they make for a truly fantastic ww2 strategy game.
Simply put, a CoH2 match is a sight to behold. You set up a machine gun to look over an important intersection, which create a kill zone. Wave after wave of enemy advances are repelled. Then, a mortar throws smoke canisters in the intersection. Enemy infantry advances through smoke, unseen,  into grenade range and dislodges your MG. They might capture it and turn it around on you. Meanwhile, elsewhere on the map, a line of sandbags allows your infantry to hold their ground against superior enemy numbers, buying time until you respond with something heavier. Somewhere offscreen, you hear an engineer screaming that they are under attack. Out of nowhere, tanks come crashing through a stone wall, allowing infantry to pour through what you thought was a sealed approach. Red flares suddenly light up an area,  signaling an imminent heavy artillery strike. You bring up a military-style map with unit icons giving you the  overview of the entire battlefield. Using it you spot an opening for your flamethrower engineers. They manage to flush out garrisoned infantry from a house and you can now capture the point. A recon airplane scours the field overhead, revealing enemy positions. Mortars and artillery pepper the more contested spots, and over time craters are formed that can now be used by your troops as cover. A Panzer attempts to navigate around a metal barricade but hits a mine - it is now immobile. Several bazooka shots bounce off its frontal armour, until you maneuver a tank destroyer from the side. It finishes off the tank from a safe range. Your tank destroyer has now gained enough experience to become a veteran, making it more accurate and hard-hitting in the future. A smouldering wreck is left where the tank once stood, thick black smoke obscuring vision in the area. Later in the match, the more resource starved Germans will maybe be able to salvage a bit of fuel from the wreck. You get the idea.
The game is not a full simulation (this is most notable in weapon and sight ranges, which are reduced from reality) but it is quite authentic nonetheless and gives of an atmosphere of a high-budget war film. All units behave as you'd expect (a Panther costs more and is stronger than a Sherman, etc.). Technically, the game looks and sounds positively stunning, sound direction is especially top notch.
All this is not to say the game is perfect. In my opinion there are three main reasons that made this game get somewhat poorer reviews than it otherwise deserves.
If you are a fan of RTS games, do not have a potato for gfx card, and you happen to like games where a tactical approach and thinking ahead are more important than high click speed - you definitely need to at least give this game a shot. If you buy it make sure to grab the Master Collection (or even better,  Franchise Pack, because CoH1 was and still is a fantastic game) for cheap during a sale, because a ridiculous amount of content was added later.

LISA is like what would happen if Earthbound (Mother2) and Space Funeral had a baby and raised it in a post apocalyptic setting. Overall I was pretty pleased with the game and would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys RPGs.

I have read over the reviews posted by other gamers like myself and I have come to a conclusion after 50 hours of gameplay.
Let's be honest here, the game is fun. Company of Heroes 2 became one of those games that really hooked me on when I first started playing it. But after playing the Russian and German factions for over 25 hours in total, I realized that the allies are always at a significant disadvantage when going up against the axis powers. The axis faction can shut down the allies easily 10 minutes into the game. I won't get into the specifics but for those who are new to the game like myself, they will understand the frustrations of playing against the Germans.
I wanted to prove myself wrong by saying: "No... there's no way that Germans can win easily 75% of the time. I must be new and that's why I still don't understand the game mechanics and how to properly use them." But sadly... that's not the case. I tried playing as the Wehrmacht and the West Obercommando factions. And I have won 7/10 times as them while playing against lv80+ ranking players. Like I said, I am pretty new to this game and I have no prior knowledge of how this game functions and how it plays out. But even a newbie like myself, playing as a German faction and able to win against high level allied players with rare commanders selected...that tells me something is awfully not balanced between the Germans and the allies.
One thing to note is, just as previously stated above, the matchmaking system is confusing to understand. How in the hell can a low level (like myself) get paired up against lv100s when it's very clear there's a skill difference between the two? There needs to be a change to the mm system because right now it is completly broken. It drives new players away. It's like putting Silver Elite Masters and Global Elites together in the same game (csgo terms). How is that fair?
This game has the potential to turn it around and set on the right track IF the developers are noticing the problems. Because after reading other reviews, I can definitely say I am not alone on this matter.
Rating: 5/10.
Unless they start to turn it around and make it more balanced, I would not recommend this game to anyone. If you really want to buy it (with the current state that it is in), then at least wait for a sale. Because right now... not even rats would want to pay for the full price.

FTL: Faster Than Light was made by Subset Games, the team consists of TWO game designers! Matthew Davis and Justin Ma, who were once members of 2K Games' Shanghai studio. The gaming world has changed a lot over the years, many AAA games have teams of a hundred or more members at times. Which just goes to show what an accomplishment FTL really is.
FTL is a roguelike strategic space exploration/combat/ship and crew management game. The mechanics of the game are very simple to learn, and endlessly fun to play. You start the game with a crew that you will have manning various stations on your ship. One crew member as the pilot, another that mans the ship's weapons station, another the shields, engine room, etc. Your crew is also used to defend the ship from intruders that are beamed over during the heat of battle with an enemy ship, or ambush your ship and board it while you pass through a system. Your crew is also important because they are also there to repair any damage done to your ship and its various systems (and believe me, they will get damaged). Keeping your crew alive and well is paramount, so when they are hurt, make sure to send them to your ship infirmary to get patched up.
As you go through the game, your crew will get better at the stations in which they work, making them more efficient. If they are doing a lot of repairs, then their speed at repairing your ship systems, hull breaches, and putting out fires will increase. Having a skilled crew becomes extremely important as you near the end of the game.
At the beginning of the game, you will choose your ship. At first, not much will be available, but as you get through the game, you will unlock more ships to use.
You aquire a resource called "Scrap" from encounters with enemies, and doing other tasks like saving merchants from space pirates, or scavenging wrecked ships, as well as many other encounters you will run into during your travels. This Scrap is used to upgrade the various systems of your ship, like its shields, weapons, engines, and every other system your ship has. You can even upgrade the internal doors of the ship to better protect the various sections from intruders who board it.
Throughout the game, you will scavenge new weapons, and other useful tools thta can be attached to your ship and used during battle, or to aid in the ship's repair. There are many different modules that can really make every play through a unique experience and give you a chance to really experiment with different builds.
While playing the game, you use your ship's FTL (Faster Than Light) drive to jump from one system to the next, trying to outrun a rebel fleet which is sweeping through the galaxy. If they catch up to you, you are a dead man as your single ship will be completely destroyed by the fleet.
FTL has you running from one end of the galaxy to the other trying to keep important data away from the rebels. This keeps you on the edge of your seat and forces you to make difficult decisions throughout the game. You won't have time or enough fuel to explore every proceedurally generated system/encounter. So, you have to really cherry pick what places you want to visit in each system before moving on to the next, but don't spend too much time in one system or the rebel fleet will catch up to you.
Because the game is proceedurally generated each time you play, each play through is completely different from the previous run, this keeps the game fresh and interesting, and makes encounters in space impossible to predict.
The game is filled with various different races, humans, mantis, and others. Members of each can be recruited at a myriad of shops, or you might save one from being marooned on a deserted planet and they might join your crew out of thanks for saving them. There are many more possibilities, and getting a new member of the crew is always a great feeling, because with more crew, the more efficiently your ship will run, and the more chance you have of surviving.
Ship combat is a strategic affair. You must keep your ship in working order, while your crew members man their specific stations. But, if you are damaged, you will have to have one of them jump off of their station to go and make repairs. If the fight isn't going your way, you may end up having all of your crew making repairs while the enemy hammers you with missiles and laser cannons.
While you are trying to keep your ship from being blown out of the stars, you will also be trying to destroy your enemy's ship as well. What is really fun about the combat in this game, is that you are able to target specific parts of the enemy ship to fire on, whether it be their shields to make them more vulnerable, or their engines so that they enemy cannot escape by firing up their own FTL drive. What I like to do is take out their weapons and then their O2(the ship's life support systems) this not only makes the enemy unable to fire on me with their own weapons, but forces them to scramble to repair their life support systems or the entire crew will suffocate! While they are attending to the frantic repairs, I pick apart the ship one system at a time until the hull cannot take anymore, and all that is left of my enemy is super heated scrap metal.
I don't want to go too in depth as to what happens when you reach the end of the game, or the challenges you will face as I don't want to ruin the fun for you. But, I can tell you that FTL is absolutely worth the low price it asks for. It will give you hours of entertainment especially if you are a science fiction fan, someone who always wanted to command your own starship in battle. This is the game for you.
Check out FLT: Faster Than Light, you will not be disappointed, I highly recommend it!

Metro 2033 Redux es un juego de estilo post apocalíptico que esta centralizado en las vías subterráneas del metro en la capital rusa, Moscow, la historia se desenlaza alrededor de Artyom, un joven a quien le encomiendan entregar un importante mensaje al comandante Miller después de repetitivos ataques a su hogar por bestias del subterráneo y por una fuerza misteriosa.
Quede sorprendido con lo increíble que se ve la superficie en esta versión remasterizada, hay un gran detalle en los edificios destruidos y desolados a tu alrededor mientras escuchas los aullidos y gritos de las bestias, la ventisca ya no se ve como si estuviera estática, tiene un movimiento fluido y constante, esto también se puede decir en cuanto al movimiento de los personajes, el subterráneo tiene una atmósfera profunda y sombría en donde sientes que son pocos en los que puedes confiar y que cualquier error en tu viaje te puede traer la perdición.
Considero bastante interesante como se relacionan las estaciones unas con otras, ya que algunas de las estaciones son independientes, mientras que otras hacen una unión para ver por el futuro de la humanidad, y otras se unen para tomar el dominio total. El juego hace un gran énfasis en este tema así que no vas a perderte nada, en especial si decides jugar las secuelas. Lamentablemente, Metro 2033 Redux no tiene muchos personajes memorables, y los que tiene, no vas a conseguir el suficiente tiempo para admirarlos ya que los personajes van y vienen a lo largo de la historia, algunas veces no llegas ni a conocer el nombre de la persona con la que estás hablando cuando prosigues con la historia.
Ademas de los bandidos y las distintas facciones que quieren el dominio total, existe una pequeña variedad de bestias mutantes los cuales resaltan perfectamente con la atmósfera sombría que el juego proporciona, criaturas pálidas que vienen de la superficie para buscar alimento, mientras que al mismo tiempo escapan de un depredador volador que no solo tiene apetito por personas y en las profundidades mas oscuras del subterráneo se encuentran arañas con una mecánica única, al encontrarte con estas arañas, lo único que tienes que hacer es iluminarlas mientras te proteges las espaldas, ya que estas están tan acostumbradas a la oscuridad que cualquier tipo de luz les inflige daño, esto es algo que nunca había visto. Lo único que no me gusto fue la masa verde que te encuentras al final del juego, es algo muy simple.
La jugabilidad es lo que mas resalta de este juego, ya que el juego te da varias opciones en las que puedes  progresar en el juego, puedes ser silencioso y pasar por los túneles sin que nadie te detecte o puedes arrasar con todo sin que nadie escuche un soplido, también puedes jugar al estilo Rambo y abrir fuego a todo el que se te ponga en frente.
Esta clase de libertad es lo que hace que el juego sea tan bueno, ya que Artyom, tu personaje, solo es un joven que tiene que entregar un mensaje, el no esta involucrado con las facciones, no es un asesino, pero tampoco puede dejar que lo eliminen, asi que esta en ti decidir el futuro de las personas con las que te encuentras.
La música en este juego es excelente y se adapta muy bien a la forma en la que estas jugando. No se siente fuera de todo ni repetitivo, y puede llegar a aumentar el todo de suspenso en algunas partes.
3/5
La historia tiene sus fallas pero esto se compensa con la buena atmósfera que te proporciona y la gran atención en los detalles, aunque me hubiera gustado que Artyom tuviera algún dialogo ya que las únicas veces que habla es en medio de las pantallas de cargas y unos comentarios en algunos libros que te encuentras esparcidos en los capítulos, un dialogo directo con los personajes hubiera estado mejor en mi opinión.

Drawn: The Painted Tower has you exploring a mysterious tower whose environments are presented as a series of screens that don't have animated objects within. You solve puzzles and explore by using your cursor to hover over key points of interest and to interact with objects. There are pictures or areas within pictures and puzzles are presented with virtually no text or, at the very most, a few cryptic clues to give you a vague idea of what to do. Your ultimate aim is to reach the top. There is a trial and error feel about the game but it gives the player a decent enough workout for the brain.
Drawn: The Painted Tower is a moody, atmospheric game which is put across immediately by its eerie main-menu. To sombre and mournful tones, a choir sings gentle choral notes in the background as if in a peaceful monastery. We also see the stone carving of Iris - the protagonist of the story - appear before us in a sad, pale turquoise colour. All of which sets a suitable tone adding to the mystery and dark nature of the game which has an almost dream-like quality.  It's more of an adventure game than a hidden object game and like many adventure games doesn't tell you how far you've progressed or how far you have to go. Although there are objectives to fulfil and it keeps you informed, there are no records kept or tabs kept on chapters. When you fire up the game, you're thrown in immediately from where you finished the previous session.
Adventure games can be obscure and downright nonsensical while others can be too text-heavy or contain overlong and repetitive dialogue trees. Thankfully a few come along that seem kinder to us noobs and a bit gentler but which still manage to be challenging enough for us to be entertained. This is one such game. Granted, although there is an option to skip the puzzles (and there is a very nice hint system), I personally only felt the need to skip two which I found too tricky.
5/5

It's a shame that this game only gets 'Mostly Positive' and even recently 'Mixed' reviews.
I played a fair bit of the original Company of Heroes, and moved over to the second during the early beta. At the time it felt like an incredibly different game, and part of me rejected it outright. However, since playing it for longer I really feel like nothing drastic has changed and the output has been a very fun and engaging RTS.
The gameplay itself is excellent. Unlike some other RTS games like C&C the gameplay is focused much more on micro-play; the way you position your units can win or lose you a game. That's fine, because that's what the majority of the game is focused on. You could have the greatest timings for building up your economy and 'teching' up; but if you leave your big♥♥♥♥♥tank with its♥♥♥♥♥♥hanging out then a couple of AT guns, which aren't all that expensive and quickly available, will leave you wish a massive hole in your army. Cover differentiates between negative, none, medium and heavy. The better the cover, the less damage your unit takes. This made everything feel a little bit more focused on the engagements you had, which were happening almost constantly across the map. Despite this, the game's pace feels very relaxed in comparison to other RTS games like Starcraft. You will feel overwhelmed at first but once you get a build order sorted (many are available online) you can forget about the whole macro strategy and focus more on getting your micromanagement up to speed.
There's a good variety of maps, each of which have their own unique personalities and promote, to a minimal degree, a different approach of play. Some buildings are very open field whereas others are heavily laden with buildings you can jump in and out of. So in an open field map you may want to consider how you're going to advance on the enemy; smoke grenades, mortar fire, artillery, a tank line? You have to think on your feet a lot; so when things go well you are very satisfied.
There is a learning curve, you need to have a quick google and glance at places like
or other wikis that explain the different capabilities of units. This is all part of learning a competitive game, and if you like the WW2 theme and the looks of the gameplay then it's well worth the invested time.
A lot of the negative reviews stem from issues of 'balance'. I think these are entirely nonsense. The balance in Company of Heroes 2 is entirely reasonable with no clear steam-rolling from any one faction. Once the British were released people♥♥♥♥♥♥themselves into thinking they were overpowered because they had no idea how to play. Shortly after, however, players figured out that the Wehrmacht faction's lone sniper unit (an early available unit) could almost negate the British player early on. Everything since has been patched. There will be strategies you find hard to deal with, or some that seem overpowered. However, that is entirely due to the fact that commanders can be used in ways others haven't thought of (even the devs, they're only human) and so rely on the community reporting these worries.
To give an example: Last night I was thrown a curve ball in a 2v2 match where the enemy built nothing but engineers. They attempted to quickly capture the map against the slow-moving British units and rushed for light tanks and vehicles which the British take a little longer to get going. Honestly, I know a lot of players who would have said "♥♥♥♥ it! These Germans are so OP!". But after capturing their territory that connects the others together (and so denies them resources) we quickly caught back up and gave them a run for their money. It was a fairly normal game (around 30 minutes) because as shocking and powerful their strategy appeared they usually have a hole to exploit which was their lack of focus on anti-tank by trying to get the early-game victory.
Don't let the balance/RNG posts fool you! Relic fairly frequently come off feedback from the community and alter balance; something it works, sometimes not - it was no different in CoH1 as notalgic reviewers like to claim. The game is fantastic and a gem. It's a shame that people protested enough to get rid of some exciting features. There used to be a blizzard mechanic that caused the maps to become bitter cold and lack visibility. Getting units to heat was a must, it slowed down the game pace but I felt it offered a unique style of play where you were rewarded for managing to be mobile during this period or using your time wisely to recoup. You could always veto these maps anyway!
All in all. Good game, give it a whirl, ignore bitter players.
