This game looked interesting.
I wish I could have experienced it.
You see, the game itself goes by a principle of 'your game is affected by other people'. That is, there's a small galaxy map, and as people blast through the levels, they eventually get 'completed' (conquered) and then those levels are CLOSED OFF until the next 'round' (which resets everything).
Each time I logged into the game to try to play it (about every 2-4 days), the 3000-4000 players that i kept seeing online had blasted through EVERYTHING and were at the final enemy homeworlds, thus locking me out of all of the other content. This happened 3 times in a row.
I am not going to pay for a game that I cannot play unless I sit in front of my computer all day waiting for the game to roll over on a map restart. There are better built games out there than this.

Helldivers should have been one of the best games around.
When you play, with a good crew, you actually feel like a special operator, dropping in from orbit on surgical strike missions and getting out as fast you can.
When you're with a bad team, it's more frustrating than any other game you can ever play.
The game is supposed to be about rapid mobility. When a team does that, even max difficulty tank killer levels are fun. Too many players try and bog themselves down in pointless last stands and too many players refuse to take risks like calling nukes on themselves or abandoning downed team mates you'll never revive in time.
The "git good" nonsense aside, the fact that the camera won't advance until all players are moving at the same time is horrible. You can't see anything, making scouting next to impossible. Sure, you have to work as a team, but the camera won't advance if a team member is downed either, so you have to wait for them to die or get them up. If you're running that fast and someone is downed, the whole team is next.
The aiming is ok, but the reticle when your weapon isn't in the shoulder is conducive to NDs in to the back of someone's head. You spend half the time trying to figure out whether or not you're going to take a player's head off by accident every time you aim a shot (Devs, maybe make the reticle more obvious/brighter). But the whole game is centred around the universe being cruel and capricious, so too bad I guess.
It's the best game and the worst game at the same time. I don't know whether our puny human brains aren't advanced enough yet to be at a competitive level with this game or I'm just not good.
I've never hated and loved a game at the same time so much in my entire life.

In the year 20XX, a former employee of Capcom shows his previous employers how to properly honor one of their own franchises as well as a truly great era of gaming, all while keeping the price tag under $2. Enter Gunman Clive.
Gameplay:
Alright, well the game isn't ENTIRELY based around Mega Man style gameplay, more-so of its level design. The levels feel very reminiscent of Capcom's classic series, and were a joy to platform through; though there were a few levels that changed things up, such as a minecart level (Donkey Kong Country here) and a shooter level somewhat similar to that of Gradius. Otherwise, it sticks to the solid jumping and shooting formula of games past and executes it well. A couple mechanics here and there could have been explored further, such as the destructible bridges, which were only in one level.  Also, the controls were also pretty responsive and translated well onto the keyboard, they are also rebindable.
Where the differences from Mega Man really appear are the weapons. The weapons operate on a system more akin to the Contra series, where you can find upgrades for your basic gun that give it a new ability. Examples would be the classic spread shot, a slow explosive shot, to even a wall-piercing laser as well as a few others; like Contra, these are lost upon taking a hit. One change to these is that how you get them is a little randomized; some are static within a level, some you can get by chance from killing an enemy. The enemies also vary from generic bandits, to ducks and seagulls, to even some strange otherworldly enemies. The bosses are also a little more similar to something like Contra rather than Mega Man, as you don't end up absorbing their abilities or anything of the like, and also aren't all exactly memorable.
Unlike Contra, however, you can take multiple hits without dying and have unlimited lives. The amount of hits you can take is dependent on the difficulty level selected. The hit detection in the game is pretty well done and I hardly ever felt I got any “cheap” deaths. There are also somewhat randomized cakes (similar to the random-ish weapons) that replenish your health. Speaking of health, one minor complaint is while the health UI is simple and non-intrusive, it only really gives you a general sense of how many hits you can take before death, rather than something more clear.
Also on the topic of UI, sadly, for you speedrunners and achievement hunters, there is no restart button on the pause menu; so if you know messed up on getting the "Star" time for that level or a "No Damage" run, you must either kill yourself (contributing to your death count) or exit the game and re-select that level. Another minor annoyance, but said speedrunning and achievements honestly kept my game time from being longer than about an hour.
One good thing for you guys is the helpful timer at the top of the screen for getting those pesky “Star” times. However, a nitpick as it may be, I wish there was an option to turn this off. This wish isn’t to benefit me or other achievement hunters, but to those who don’t care about those kinds of things and who just want to spend an hour to play through the game and not have to feel some sort of false pressure of a ticking clock. Otherwise it’s much more helpful than hurtful for replayability, it would just be nice to have the option to opt-out of it.
Speaking of replayability, there are two extra modes, one where you play as the damsel-in-distress herself, Ms. Johnson, with her ability to float (Super Mario Bros. 2 here); as well as a humorous Duck Mode in which you play a defenseless duck with the ability to fly upwards for a short bit. These feature a few more achievements on top of Clive's own No Death, Time-Trial, and No Damage ones. These alone probably increased my play time by four-fold and were pretty enjoyable.
Graphics:
To quote the game's trailer, the game features "Weird Artsy-Looking 3D Graphics", which is more or less true. As you can see, it has an interesting sketch-book like aesthetic on top of the dominant western theme. Personally, the lack of color was not an issue for me, due to the game's length; and towards the later levels, while the continued use of brown could be seen as lazy, I felt it made the levels a little more surreal. In general, the model quality and animations were done pretty well too.
As an added bonus to being on PC, we also get 1080p 60fps gameplay as well as some super-sampling, making this the definitive version in regards to graphics (unless you want the 3D effect of the 3DS.)
One very small detail used in the game's graphics was how objects that did have color bled a little color through the outlines or weren’t completely filled in, especially when the screen was moving. This was a cool trick to make the game bare resemblance to a water-painting, again re-emphasizing the whole "Artsy-Looking" theme. There were probably some other tricks used that even I didn't pick up on.
And an even smaller detail about the graphics (that may not even be on purpose), and I'm probably only one to make this comparison, but to me at least, sometimes when Clive dies or gets hit, the pose he makes bears some resemblance to the death screen of Zelda II. It could just be me, but as supportive evidence, you eventually fight what appears to be a "dark" version of Clive himself, much similar to the final boss of Zelda II. Ironically, he is very easy, unlike in the NES game.
Sound:
The music more or less fits the western style of the game, and gives it a bit more atmosphere. The tracks generally range from "okay" to "pretty good" to easily sum them up. Also, toward the end levels, the music begins to become a bit more chiptune-like, similar to that of the games inspired by it. The music is also composed by the creator’s brother, so this is not an entirely one-man effort.
Story:
Clive himself is a man of few words, none at all actually. With a tagline like "In the year 18XX", you pretty much know what you're in for on a story level. Kill the bandits, shoot some ducks, save the girl, become a duck. It's simple and it works.
There is a possibility that there is a little more at play than what the story is on paper, such as how pretty much all of the stores are suspiciously owned by Mayor Johnson and named after him, but that could just be me trying to bring meaning to something meaningless.
Now to the biggest overall complaint about the game: the length. I myself finished my first run through on Normal at around an hour. Then my first run without dying was about 16 minutes. The game is not heavy on content, more-so on replayability, but what is there is well-crafted and polished.
And while its own trailer makes self-deprecating remarks such as "A Generic Old School Side-Scroller" with "Lots of Brown", this doesn't mean it is not well executed and that brown isn't put to damn good use.

One of my favorite platformers, very reminiscent of Megaman in gameplay and old western movies in looks. The different styles of gameplay are also cool and add some replayability.

Gameplay: The game is a straightforward run n' gun platformer. Kind of like Mega Man if Mega Man forsook all his trademark abilities for Contra-esque weapon pickups such as spread guns and bouncing bullets. The game definitely lifts some elements from other old-school games as well such as disappearing blocks and Mario firebars. The game is 20 levels long, but the levels are very short and are mostly more like checkpoints then actual thematically-divided levels.
Graphics: The game is 3D with simple models, but also some kind of hand-drawn filter over everything that makes it look very visually appealing, if a little monochrome.
Sound: Easily the weakest part of the game. There's only a handful of music tracks, and they're all pretty forgettable. The sound, meanwhile, is all just a handful of bleeps and bloops, but the worst offense in this department is when things happen that should be accompanied by sound but aren't. Boss entrances are the most affected by this. It's really jarring seeing a steam train transform into a giant robot and do so COMPLETELY SILENTLY.
Story: About as much as your average NES platformer. A short intro sequence. A short ending sequence. Maybe a short scene somewhere in the middle. A generic "save the princess" plot (or Ms. Johnson in this case.) You know the drill.
Longetivity and Replayability: I beat the whole game in less than an hour on my first try. However, there are multiple difficulty modes and two other playable characters with different play styles.
Final Verdict: It's short and there's some sound issues, but for $2 it's worth picking up and giving a try.

I've loved this game, i'm not as old as many are, so i would didn't play it when it released, as a matter of fact, i played it in the middle of 2014, i had some bad feelings, since the graphics were not as good as today's games are, but i understood it since it was old and i didn't care much for graphics anyway.
The story is amazing, you are a newborn vampire, thrown in a world where you don't know who made you a vampire, and wake up in the middle of a conflict, between the ones who keep the masquerade together and some vampires(The masquerade is the way vampires have not to show themselves to people, should anyone break the masquerade rules, such as turning someone into a vampire, showing his or her powers to humans and so, will be assasinated by the Camarilla, who are somewhat vampire police). Then you fight your way through the hordes of vampires with  Jack, a brujah.
After that you pretty much make the game yourself. Whether you want to help the camarilla or the anarchist is your choice, and the endings are many, i don't want to spoil much of the history, but it is a great history.
In the character making you get to choose between seven vampire clans, each with their own abilities and specializations. After that you proceed to distribute your points in each skill, such as hacking, lockpicking, strength Etc...
This game follows the levelling system really REALLY like a old table RPG, having many skills and giving you a good number of points each level up, it's like dark souls, only its points instead of souls and there are many more skills.
Then comes the character, the protagonist is pretty much made by you, since you choose his answers, who he will or not help(or kill) and whether he wants to follow the masquerade or not. However there are other characters important to the game, such as Sebastian Lacroix, an old vampire who is the current leader of the Camarilla, Nines Rodriguez a brujah who is an anarchist, and as a matter of fact the leader of the "Anarchist Crew" and on and on. All the important characters have a very good voice acting, and the less important ones and simple citizens in the streets are decent.
Do not let yourself be pushed away by the graphics or age of this game, it is truly great and it made it's way into my second favorite game out of a Steam library with more than 200 games(and thats not taking into account the games i played in console), only being surpassed by Deus Ex: Human Revolution.

King Arthur's Gold, or KAG, is a game set in the Dark Ages, with common controls. It currently has three available classes, Knight, Archer, and Builder. The Knight has a sword and shield. You can hold down to have a strong sweep, or click for a simple stab. Holding down the left mouse button long enough will result in a glimmer which signals that you can make two strong sweeps. The Knight can also purchase bombs, which help destroy terrain, and water bombs, which stun enemies. The Archer has a bow and grappling hook. The grappling hook has a range of about 7 blocks, and pulls the player towards the block it has latched onto. The player can also move and climb while latched, and can also fire arrows. The archer has multiple types of arrows, including fire, which can set fire to wooden structures and players, and bomb arrows. The builder has the ability to build traps, obstacles, fortresses, and large-scale weapons such as a catapult.
I personally enjoyed KAG, not to an addictive rate, but I still enjoyed playing the small campaign, creating in the sandbox, and playing multiplayer. There are modded servers for KAG, which I have not currently tried as of yet. I think it was a fairly good game, but would not reach my top 10. I recommend it for my friends with weaker computers, however, because it has fairly good graphics, small world generation, and high FPS. I do recommend this game, but not as much as some others.

This game is clearly patterned after AdCap, but not a total clone. For one thing, the balance values appear to be different.
However the game has one clear killer to it. It stores its data to a local drive file, and apparently keeps it open during execution. This means that is you do not shut the game down cleanly (such as if you have a power outage or a blue screen), the save file is corrupted, and the game will hang while trying to load it. The only known fix is to delete your save file, which loses all progress you have made to that point. For a long-term game such as this that is unacceptable.
Should they ever fix this issue, then it might be a fun game to play in the background.

Do not let the fact that this game is made in RPG Maker fool you.  LISA is a game worth the money I put into it.
The game's humor and characters are well designed and each of them have their own quirks and those quirks end up being used in battle a lot.  For example, one of the characters talks a whole lot and that quirk is used in battle.
The art style and world design is completely different.  Instead of a top-down view you would see for most RPG Maker games this game uses a side view where you can jump up and down platforms and climb up and down ropes.  Falling damage is also in this game depending on height.
The game's choices are, in a way, a little harder than you would see from other choices.  One such example is the choice from losing your party member or lose all your money and items.  Either of them carry a certain weight that has to be taken to perspective.
All and all I would wholly recommend this game to anyone looking for something weird and entertaining.

The proverbial Starship Troopers game we forgot we wanted since the 90's.
The Good:
-General combat.
-DLC. The weapons you can pick up in DLC are fun and can help make things a little easier (boots for example, a Sickle to start with) but they're complimentary to the weapons and stratagems in the game. Of course there are weapon oddities that skewer the meta. I know the AR-20L is the best main weapon but I prefer my LAS-5 Scythe for solo jobs.
-The difficulty spike. It's pretty fair in comparison to a lot of other games out there until you hit Rank 10 and above. Then it throws bigger curve balls.
-Co-op Danger: Teams have to work together well in order for the game to not screw you. I like that it is easy for you and your squad to kill each other and with mob overload how fast they can table you if you get careless.
- The gear levelling system/research mechanic. It lets you customise your gear well.
The Bad:
-The grind/replayability factor. After beating bosses and helping win a few of the galactic wars the game lost its charm as the grind set in.
The Mixed:
-Characterisation. The general theme of the game is excellent however it all seems remarkably flat and generally hit and miss. Yeah, I'd have liked the option to know more on a few ocassions.
- The Galactic Wars. A great idea that is hard to capitalise on. What's that, done for the night on that world with that stratagem you really want? Oh, that world's gone an hour later if you warp away or what have you. And it's harder to gear up for people when the push is on for an enemy's capital. Add to that the grind factor and it kind of kills the game.
- The camera angle. I see a lot of complaints about this and while it's not perfect I don't mind it too much, would it have worked better with LT/RT camera angle changes like in XCOM? Maybe. Who knows?
All in all, I loved Helldivers and got a lot of playtime out of the game and can't help but recommend it for co-op shenanigans. Shredder Missiles are for life, not just for Super Christmas.

Gunman Clive was a game that I had owned on my 3DS when it launched, however when the Steam Holiday Auction happened, I went to go see what games were very low on bids before the event closed for the day. I just happened to see this game that I never knew was on Steam.
Gunman Clive is an old-school style Run n' Gun game very similar to games such as Mega Man, set in the old west in the days of the cowboys. Your overall mission of the game is to save the maiden and defeat her kidnapper.

+ Great soundtrack.

+ Vast array of different weapons that drop from enemies (Reminds me of Contra).
+ Levels are short and provide a good challenge (Great for speed running, not great for people looking for a longer game).
+ Great visuals, hand drawn artstyle really fit the game.
Cons:
- More of a personal thought, I felt this game took too much inspiration from games like Mega Man, such as stage elements.
- Game is pretty dang short. The normal game itself is only about a hour long and even with other modes, 100% this game will only take you up four hours max. In the main game, there are only 20 levels.
Final Thoughts:
~ Game has great features such as its soundtrack, gameplay, and visuals. However, the game's only has one standout problem, the Length. However, for it's cheap price, this game is a must have. I can only hope Gunman Clive 2 comes to PC.
Final Score: 8.5/10

A Gentleman Gamer's Review of "Gunman Clive," developed by “Hörberg Productions”
Introduction:
- Gunman Clive is a 2D, action platformer in tune with the Mega Man games (i.e. Jump and Shoot)  to give an example. However, GC (Gunman Clive) adds a Western/Steam Punk twist to the beloved genre.
Plot Summary:
- It is 18XX, you are a gunman named Clive (hence the title) and are tasked to rescue the Mayor's daughter/your love interes, Ms. Johnson, from bandits that have kidnapped her; however, there is an other wordly influence to this crime. You must jump and shoot your way throug platforms, enemies and bosses with your cowboy, gunslinger abilities!
Presentation:
- The first thing to catch your eye in GC is its unique art style. It is stylized in a sketch artstyle; this somehow enhances the spaghetti western feel due to it making it seem more vintage and stylized. The use of differents shades of brown screams the west. Secondly, the music is what you would expect in a western. The music fits the mood perfectly; at times, it is very reminiscent to some of Mega Man's soundtrack, giving it a high octane feel. Genre and setting truly mesh well together; being a cowboy and all it just makes sense.
Gameplay & Mechanics:
- GC offers some variety to its gameplay. From the beginning, as it is custom gaming etiquette, you are allowed to choose your difficulty; however, you can choose to play as Clive or Ms. Johnson (more options unlocked upon finishing the game). They differ from gameplay. Clive is faster and can run and gun; whereas, Ms. Johnson cannot but can float decend slowly; very much like Peach's float ability from Super Mario Bros. 2 (USA). The layout of the levels feel like a mixture of Mega Man and Metal Slug level design (so I can make a point of reference). There are enemies in cover and you can take cover as well. You must do platforming challenges; the infamous knockback deaths are present in this action platformer; however, it is not as intrusive as in other Nintendo classics. Unlike the Blue Bomber (Mega Man), you acquire power ups via random drops and they are only temporary. The game itself is fairly challenging but nothing too difficult. Unfortunately, its on the short side, paying homage to other classic games.
Final Thoughts:
- As I look over my experience of this game, it was rather enjoyable. Eventhough, its rather short (I was able to beat the game for my first time under a hour), I picked it up again literally after I have just finished it to rank the levels and try out the other characters. If you asked me if it has replayability, its a definite yes from me. If the length concerns you, the low price is more than justifiable (especially because I bought it on sale when the game is already so low priced). Gunman Clive is the perfect homage to NES Megaman games and classic games in general. Had lots of fun; I'm sure you will too.
PS:
- If you'd enjoyed this game like I did, I would have you know that there is a recent sequel on 3DS. Hopefully, it will get ported to PC like this one

LISA is  my surprise game of the year. There is no higher praise I can give a game this compelling.
LISA clearly draws inspiration from the phenomenal Earthbound series on the SNES. However, that's not to say this title isn't worthy of the grand world of PC Gaming.
This game plays a lot like Earthbound in the sense of the combat, level progression, exploration, and overall feel. You feel a sense that things are inspired by Earthbound, but LISA expands on this in a meaningful way and takes it in its own direction. That being said, LISA as a whole treads a much darker path than Earthbound. That's not to say that this game doesn't have its subtleties as well , I found the story to be incredibly deep.
LISA's beauty is that it does a lot of groundbreaking things with a relatively simple, yet elegant canvas. No console could contain the things this game does.
If you are curious -> buy it. Just remember to save often and avoid strolling off the cliff after the introduction and you'll have a hell of a time.

I don't normally write reviews, but I just couldn't resist writing one for this game!
Two words: "absolutely fantastic". I honestly can't even remember the last time I've played a game that left me this... Satisfied. Yes, it can be difficult in some areas, some fights are harder than others, so it definitely earns its title of "a painful RPG"! (Nothing a little grinding could not fix, though) "Painful" is just the start of it, honestly. You think you're safe to have a rest in this little tent a stranger so generously offered to you? Think again! A multitude of things might happen - you might get beaten, harassed, molested, or a secret admirer might leave you a present. Decided to take a break under the starlit sky, after that one difficult fight? Well, I hope you'll be glad to hear that one of your comrades got kidnapped for ransom. What will you do now? Pay the ransom? Or abandon your battle brother to the tides of destiny? It's all up to you.
This game, while unforgiving in some aspects, almost always gives you a choice. (Some of these so-called "roadblocks" can be a bit disheartening, but they add to the overall plot quite nicely) Each area is unique and filled with a different cast of characters! Some depressed, some angry and aggresive, some down-right weird and perverted. While some recruitable characters do not have a lot of dialogue tied to them, they're all unique in their own way, with a little backstory behind each of them.
Exploration is always rewarded. Of course, it depends on your definition of "reward" - a worthy enemy to test your mettle against, or perhaps a hidden treasure in one of the darkest recesses of a cave? Who knows, you might discover something you'd never have expected to find! It's just so pleasant to see a lot of small, intricate details dotted around the different locations.
This game also gives off a very nice Earthbound-esque vibe - from the characters and the presentation of the areas, down to the music. While the soundtrack is probably not something you'd listen to on any given regular day, it adds to the game's atmosphere incredibly well.
So, all in all, don't be afraid! Put on your time-worn poncho, gather your most trusted allies and embark on a painful quest of self-discovery, violence, perversion, drugs, craziness and most importantly - skin.

If you've been following the hype and kickstarter pitch, prepare to be disappointed.
If you're picking this up without any prior expectations going in, prepare for the best RPGMaker-based game you'll play all year, and probably ever.
LISA itself is a pretty good game. The writing is interesting and funny, the plot is actually worthwhile, the characters are amazing and diverse, and most interestingly, the combat is pretty solid. I'm amazed that I'm saying that about a turn-based RPG, especially considering how I feel about the genre(gigantic waste of ♥♥♥♥ing time).
The characters are diverse in writing... when they have something to say. Yeah, the only real problem I have with the characters is that there are too many ♥♥♥♥ing silent protagonists. They're pretty diverse in play styles, too, though, and if things get stale combat-wise you can always freshen things up by changing even just a couple of characters in your party. Accomplishing this feat with this many characters is pretty damn impressive, so hats off to LISA-man for pulling that off. The only gameplay downside is there's a few characters that... well, pretty much just have one ♥♥♥♥ing gimmick and that's all there is to their combat style.
The combat is solid and surprisingly engaging. You can chain basic attacks into combos with a lot of characters, which gives it a pretty unique feel. There's a few balancing issues(headslide OP. Headslide VERY OP.) but overall the combat is surprisingly enjoyable and I'd say that if more turn based RPGs has combat systems like this, I might not think the whole genre to be a reeking pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥
And here comes where the game disappointed me.
--SPOILERS AHEAD--
The writing is pretty funny, the atmosphere is great, but the "sacrifice" part is not well implemented. It feels kind of stupid when every major sacrifice you make in the game boils down to a pick-your-poison, unavoidable binary decision, always thrown at you by the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This is the first major shortcoming of the game. I wanted sacrifice for a reason, not sacrifice because ♥♥♥♥ you this one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hates you a lot and is basically jigsaw from SAW. It gives me the feeling that this game was kind of rushed, with the sacrifice aspect quickly crowbarred in.
If you were lead to expect a choose your own adventure kind of experience from the pre-release hype, prepare to be disappointed on that front, too, because no matter what you do you get the same ending. No matter what you do all the major plot points all pan out the same exact way with maybe two or three lines of dialogue altered to reflect choices you made. Nothing you do in LISA matters to LISA, and the plot is no less linear than any other RPG you'd play. The only thing your choices impact in the end is gameplay, and that's as old as item management is.
--END SPOILERS--
Overall, LISA has failed to live up to my expecations. It's failed to come close to meeting my expectations. That does not, however, mean it's a bad game. All it really means is don't expect the ground-breaking innovation in storytelling you were promised, because it's not here.
LISA is, in fact, a good game. It's a ♥♥♥♥ing amazing turn-based RPG game. The plot is still engaging despite its shortcomings and the combat is interesting enough to keep you playing along to the end. I would recommend this game, and I give it a 7/10

LISA. How can I talk about this game in a way that would make any kind of sense..? Well, keep reading to see me try. At it's core, I can describe LISA as Earthbound's side-scrolling creepy uncle. The game at the time of this review of mine has not recieved nearly as much attention as I feel it deserves. It's equal parts touching, funny and heartbreakingly tragic. Gone are the JRPG tropes or teen-young adult pretty boys and loli girls, in are Middle-Aged men, Luchadors and Fishmen (to name only a few replacements).
With a very powerful opening that tackles bullying and an abusive father, we're thrown into the shoes of a middle-aged balding man named Brad Armstrong and his battles with substance abuse, where the game jumped forward an unknown number of years to a post-apocalyptic reverse of the comic "Y: The Last Man" where men are the only group of people who have survived whatever incident has occured. That's when our unconventional hero Brad, comes across a little baby all wrapped up and seemingly abandoned, but in this world of only men, this child turns out to be a female. Where is the woman who gave birth to her? What is Brad to do, hand her over so when she grows up she can help repopulate the world? Protect her and let her live her own life? And that's as far as I will go with our story, as it takes many many twists and turns till we reach our end.
Gameplay wise, LISA is a turn-based RPG with an optional combo input system along the lines of Xenogears, with a large cast of recruitable characters with their own little stories and personality along the lines of Chrono Cross and Suikoden-- which is something this game has in droves, personality. The battle system is handled in a first-person perspective when selecting your moves like Earthbound, but when you active your attacks, your character will appear next to your target and strike them with the attack. You can ride around on a bike like Pokemon, there are puzzles and mini-games galore. There are events that can occur while you rest at bonfires, notes can be left for you, characters of yours can be kidnapped, mags (your currency) can be robbed from you-- there is a very small underline of survival in the game, that doesn't feel tacked on or overbearing, with more inventory management than some of the more recent survival-horror titles that have been released. The game does have some fairly tough battles that require some strategy and knowledge of the system.  I also have to note that much like older games of the same cut, there is next to no hand-holding, and there are times where you might be unsure where to head next.

LISA is also absolutely jam-packed with references and love letters to many different things. The RPG genre, Lets Players and Pro-Wrestling to name a few. The game's references resonated with my love for classic JRPGs, Matt and Pat from Best Friends Play on youtube and WWE references up the yin-yang. Things that I adore. If you love WWE, JRPGs and Crazy LPers, you'll get a kick out of the little references sprinkled throughout the game.
I've only gone through the game only once, but it begs for multiple playthoughs due to some choices that you can make during your journey, and if you've fallen in love with the game as I have, you'll want to absorb every little piece of dialogue and alternate path you can.
LISA snuck itself into my Library at the end of 2014 to crown itself game of the year in a year which featured many fantastic titles both indie and AAA alike.
Is LISA for you..? Do you want a thought provoking story? Do you want a game that will make you feel something? Do you want to laugh? Do you want to re-live the glory days of the JRPG genre? Do you want something fresh done with the JRPG genre? This game is for you.
Is LISA NOT for you..? Do you want to invest some time into a game? Do you just skip through speech to mow through a game? Are you homophobic? Do you not want to play the role of a 40-something bald man and his team of freaks and weirdos? Do you have troubles with games that don't hold your hand?  This game is probably not for you.
Clearly, the game is a 10/10 for me, and it's certainly not for everyone. LISA is my game of the year for 2014.

It's definitely worth the few megabytes and minutes to read this short story. Yet after I finished it for a while, I found myself thinking back to it. A lot of people say the story is too simple, but given time to think, the very simplicity and openness of the story to be what makes it so great. There are a lot of good stories but conciseness is a virtue. The choices in this story may just say something meaningful about life.
The first time I read it, I also thought the story was too simple and all too familiar myself. A lot of Chinese student videos and soap operas like to visit the theme of the street vending dreamer. The "bad endings" are not fleshed out. The "good ending" might not make sense at first.
But alas. I am quite the fan of these art student type stories. I like to ponder them. First, I found it amusing that the artist inserted himself into the story. Then I felt the same struggles that he must feel being an artist trying to make an impact in this world. We dream a dream so different from life. And yet life is like a dream.
I had a dream about this story. This story is like life: the life of the artist, the lives of us, choices we make, our endings in our own stories, the stories of our dreams and of our lives.
*****Spoilers below*****
The choices. Yes you either make the right choice, or you are forced to go back and then make the right choice. But these choices are they not the choices we face every day? These choices in our lives that sometimes we don't feel like we want to choose what society tells us to pick. Sure I sleep in one day, or I can not help someone out one day, but what is the path that we chart in our lives that will lead to our dreams? To be able to make the right choice when it matters, is it not best to make the right choice whether it matters or not?
The "good ending" is random. Maybe. Is life not random? Do our dreams really make so much sense? To bring together a dream and daily life, something magic has to happen. It's randomness of life that allow for dreams. The randomness of dreams that let us live. That is the ending that I found.
A story worth revisiting when I wake up again.

One of the best twin-stick shooters I've ever played. It's easy to learn, and friends can join you or drop-out mid-game (locally or online). The mechanics are solid and fun at first, but they get old as you rank up. Each "mission" requires you doing a bunch of different objectives, but you'll eventually play the game enough times that you have experienced the entire variety of objectives the game has to offer and start to feel like you're doing the same thing again and again. Harder missions just involve doing more of the same objectives with tougher and more numerous enemies present on the map. They do have other missions like boss battles and community events involving defending or attacking capital planets to change things up but you'll eventually do those enough times too until it's just the same. Also, once you've unlocked all the available stratagems and capes from the various planets in the game, have beaten each boss at least once, and experienced most of what the game has to offer, the only reason to keep playing is to grind for EXP to rank up (as there are additional items that will only be available by ranking up).

Please understand that I am NOT the best reviewer for a platformer like "Gunman Clive". I haven't played platformers much since about 1991, when the platformers of the time, with their extreme precision jumps and shots, never varying even an iota, created a feeling of a Holy Grail Quest that lasted long into the night. Now the term "platformer" is VERY different, with things like FPS platformers. Say WHAT!?
Gunman Clive. First off, I paid 99 CENTS for it, mainly because of the art. That and the incongruous images on the Store Page. Cowboys and space flight?! Sure, why not when the possibilities of that concept are nearly endless. The idea of cowboys firing ray guns from hover platforms is hard to turn one's back on, especially with such AMAZING, yet simple, art. And then one starts to play....
The right hand moves, the left jumps and shoots (so far, at least on a keyboard.) That's all you need to know. Part of the reason I now avoid platformers is some physical issues. This is not a "jumping" game. THANK YOU! Yes, you jump, and some are quite precise, but not while shooting, and flipping. while cooking an omlet and reading Moby♥♥♥♥♥♥ But that's not what this game's really about. The jumps are generally harder to MISS than to achieve. A player starts by searching for a kidnapped farmer's daughter, or some such, as either a cowboy named Gunman Clive. (Why not the more aliterative "Cowboy Clive" is a mystery) or a "Ms. Johnson", presumably the victim's mother. (VERY nice touch. I rather more enjoy the female character, with her dress-induced mincing steps, and her frequent floating to the ground, as result of said dress inflating.) A player has a choice of 3 skill levels. I haven't tried the hardest, but it seems as though the difference in the first two is mostly the amount of life one has. It's just you and you trusty 1,000 shooter. (Or some such.) You're attacked by cowboys, wolves, bunnies, ducks... Yes, ducks, too low to the ground to shoot. Usually. Sometimes shooting something results in "birthday cake" health, which shrinks in size and finally vanishes if you don't reach it in time. Or (naturally!) one of a selection of ray guns. Unfortunately, the ray gun is as hard to hold onto as it is (usually) valuable in battle.
It's true (at least for me) that some sections between save points must be played dozens of times. While this might be a dealbreaker in some games, not with Clive. Things change. A cowboy with a gun before now throws dynamites(sic), and he's GOOD! But maybe shooting him will produce a piece of cake or a ray gun. Nothing is ever exactly the same, but similar enough to encourage progress with most attemps. The differences are certainly enough to keep the game from getting boring, or excessively frustrating. The good news about achievements: GC has them. The bad news: you aren't likely to see any of them.
Hopefully this review will grow with time. I've not gotten far yet, primarily on middle skill level. If you'll excuse me, I really MUST get back to the game....

On the hunt for another game that plays like Deus Ex (open world, many ways to complete tasks, stealth is almost always an option, etc.),  I fell onto this game.  And I'm both happy and sad about it.
This game is fun, engrossing, interesting and at times a little creepy.  The setting, SoCal, becomes as much a character as any of the off the wall kindred or kine you meet.  To me, I can't get enough open world games set in present day cities, and this has to be one of the more quirky and shady settings that I've played in recent years.
The gameplay isn't as polished as a game like Deus Ex, but not many games are.  If you get past the dated graphics / character design and the not-so-great combat mechanics, you'll be able to enjoy a big world that has a lot to offer, filled with funny and odd characters throughout.
It's one of those games that after you beat it, you look forward to the next play through a year down the road.  There are a handful of different clans to play as (which can really change the way you play), but as most people suggest, save the Malkavian clan for your 2nd play through for when you already understand the story.
After you get into the game, learning the basics of the Lore that VtmB has developed over the years, you're bound to want more.  And I want so much more.  This game couldn't be big enough.  I want more chapters, more missions, more locations to explore.  More dangerous encounters.  Hell, take this engine to New York or Chicago or London.  Tell more stories using the already rich World of Darkness universe.
The huge problem with all this is that there hasn't been another video game in the Vampire: The Masquerade (or even World of Darkness) universe since this game; 2004.  With so much dense material to create a story with, it's surprising that it hasn't happened.  I'm not sure I would've been interested in the MMO that got canceled earlier this year, but it would've been better than nothing.
- If you want a game that you can take your time exploring, a game that gives you the freedom to go about completing parts of the story the way you want, and don't mind Vampires as a means of telling a story, then please, get this game.

Several options are available to the crew in deciding how to disable or destroy enemies.  Blast their hull with missiles and lasers until the ship is destroyed; Take out the enemy subsystems to reduce their combat effectiveness surgically before focussing on dealing hull damage; Send boarding parties to eliminate their crew (and reap the benefits of having more of their resources intact after the battle); Send drones to attack their ship for you; Hack their systems and lock out their rooms; Mind-control your enemies; Teleport bombs inside thier ship; Destroy their life support systems and have their crew asphyxiate; Set their ship ablaze and laugh as their crew become engulfed.
There's many options, some work better than others.  There are several strategies you can choose, but you are constrained by resources, time, fuel, ammunition, hull condition, your crew's abilities (or handicaps), and sometimes simply what the "Shop" has to sell you.
Don't like the roguelike element?  There's a simple way around it where you can load a savegame with relative ease (google it).

In light of the new Star Wars: Battlefront 2 (EA), many will likely ignore this now 12 year old (as of writing this review) game, and while that is admittedly sad, there is still reason to pick this up, especially on sale.
Star Wars is perhaps my favorite franchise of all time. Interesting and likeable characters, fascinating aliens, huge and awesome capital ships, a great and classic story. But perhaps more than that, the actual wars. Huge, large scale conflicts, turrets blasting up at the swooping fighters, engaged in deadly dogfights, tanks and walkers firing at each other, huge waves of infantry sweeping across unique and stunning locations and heroes and villians clashing in various duels of the fates. Star Wars: Battlefront II lets you live and fight in such battles, control those fighters, satisfy that childhood dream of striding across Hoth in an AT-AT, gunning down rebel scum, or perhaps as a clone in the grand army of the Republic, protecting the peace and liberty of the galaxy until the day you march into the Jedi temple and execute Order 66.
Well...sort of...but I'll explain the game a bit more first. I'll start with the basics.
This game has a practical bevy of content. The main draw is easily the 'Instant Action', you can set up a match on any of the maps, choose what era you want to play in, choose a game mode, and go. The title of this mode should say it all, no queues, no waiting, no boring opening or closing cutscenes, just jumping straight in and showing off its fun and solid gameplay. This mode rely's heavily on bots, it's biggest strength being perhaps it's biggest weakness and also brings down many of the other singleplayer modes. The AI is downright stupid, staring at walls, not running away from grenades, going into the same chokepoints again and again.
Stupid AI can be forgiven as the gameplay is still hugely fun and while the assymetrical map design adds a lot to the replayability of it all, it often piles up with the idiotic AI, to make many maps unbalanced which leads into my other problem, if you aren't the biggest fan of vehicles or heroes, tough luck as it's often the only way to win any of the matches, at least with certain sides. I love the Clone Wars Era but the clones who man the walkers are so infuriatingly dumb and slow, it can make playing the Clone Wars a nightmare. I will state that the losses on particular maps being unbalanced isn't a case of me being awful, my K/D on these bot matches is around 10 to 1, these particular losses don't feel earned, but rather cheap and infuriating as I mow down enemies by the dozen and slaughter fifty plus on a good hero streak and still lose.
The game also has a campaign mode. I'm not going to lie, the story is not very good. You follow the 501st, a legion of clones, throughout their various exploits in The Clone Wars and Galactic Civil War. The gameplay consists of multiplayer maps with objectives and special voiced lines along with starting and ending cutscenes with mini exposition dumps and skippable space battle sections. The story is bad, the storytelling is bad, the cutscenes are awful...
But you know what, I ****ing love it.
It's fun, it makes me wish that this stage and progressing objective based gameplay was a default option in Instant Action. It's not proper cannon, but it follows the general idea of the movies. I get to hold the beach on Kashyyk, I get to mow down the Jedi while my fellow clones shout "For the Chancellor!", I get to fight through the dense forests of Yavin 4 to avenge the loss of the first Death Star. It is fanservice. It is incredibly poorly presented but beautiful, lovely fanservice and I ****ing love it.
The other mode of note is Galactic Conquest. It's something of a turn based strategy mode that incorporates the regular and space gameplay, where you construct fleets, train troops, purchase bonuses and earn credits. Depending on the options you selected, victory can be achieved in a variety of ways. There isn't that much to say, given all the modes are basically the same multiplayer maps with the same Eras and bots except that Galatic Conquest is REALLY good. Taking a simple match and adding some form of longer terms stakes really ups the ante and adds a proper drive to do well. The AI who makes the tactical decisions for your enemy is also ridiculously awful and does the same thing essentially over and over again but it still provides a solid amount of fun.
The gameplay itself is pretty straight forward, pretty standard first person shooter controls with the option to play in third person. The recoil is pretty low so it isn't a hugely hard game . There are grenades, non regenerating health, secondary weapons and a stamina bar which is drained through rolling and sprinting. Vehicles, turrets and ships control pretty much as you would expect but Battlefront II's unique gameplay element are its heroes. Han Solo, Princess Leia, Luke Skywalker, Mace Windu, Aayla Secura, Darth Vader, Darth Sideous (I like to scream 'UNLIMITED POWER!' when using his lightning ability), Anikin Skywalker, Obi-Wan Kenobi and a few others. Most have a forced third person view, and lightsaber combat feels like throwing two action figures at each other, it feels so awkward that I actively avoid it completely. However, otherwise the heroes are pretty fun and it feels nice to play a lot of my favorite characters.
The multiplayer is kind of dead. There is a mod but I haven't tried it. Luckily though, the offline modes provide more than enough content for hundreds of hours worth of entertainment. I played it a lot before I got this steam account. I had played around 80 on that one so don't let my current logged hours fool you.
But speaking of mods, this game still has an active (albiet small modding community) and their various creations add tons of value to the game for free. I'll give a list here of some worth having although not all are compatible.
-Unofficial Battlefront 2 patch Version 1.3
-Rezzed Maps (Makes the maps look really good. This also fixes an isssue I'll mention in just a bit.)
-Battlefront Evolved (Updates models and textures for most heroes and units, great if you want your game to look a little newer)
-Ultimate Battlefront: The Clone Wars (Based off The Clone Wars TV show, adds new modes, new maps and a completely new Era with lots and lots of new units and heroes)
-Battlefront Extreme (Overhauls some of the gameplay and effects)
-Battlefront Conversion Pack (Adds the Old Republic Era, a lot of new maps and maps from the original Star Wars: Battlefront)
-Dark Times 2: Rising Son (I had issues with this mod  but it's pretty good overall. A must for any Galactic Civil War fan)
So now to talk of other things. Graphically, it holds up fairly well, Rezzed Maps and Battlefront Evolved improve the experience greatly and there are a few ENB style mods out there but I can't talk much of their benifits of them as have an AMD graphics card and most aren't designed for AMD and will thus not let you launch the game normally, it is possible to run it with the "testapp" application in your gamefiles but it will not count your logged hours and it's a pain to have to locate the gamefiles every time. Another problem which I briefly brought up when talking about the Rezzed Maps mod, new AMD drivers will often lead to ground texture issues, Kashyyk looks awful because the ground is a weird variety of colors and this extends to some mod maps like A Speck of Dust. Rezzed maps doesn't completely fix it, but it helps a bit for some maps like Naboo.
In other words, don't use an AMD card, unless you're willing to rollback your drivers (some ENB mods will come with compatability fixes for older crimson drivers) you're going to have to put up with Yavin 4 having red soil. This game can run on craptops too though some mods may cause some lag.
This is a classic, worth your time and money. It's fun, it's accesible. It's Star Wars.
Buy it.

Lisa is an incredible RPG where the developers spent an immense ammount of effort into building the world of Lisa.
The game has a very minimal number of conversations and cutscenes but manages to make you care about the quirky characters scattered around the world.
The conversations and characters never failed to make me laugh and there are so many little neat details used to develop them. You'll be laughing at the smallest things like the main characters tripping off a ledge. Characters range from anything from a crossdressing badass to a talking fish lawyer.
An average run of the game will take around 10-13 hours depending on how much of the optional content you see, but there's tons of replay value in finding secrets and solving mysteries that Dingaling has scattered around the world, optional dialogs, dozens of optional party members, and minigames. It's fully worth the 10 bucks and I've managed to play around 15+ hours into after finishing the game the first time.
Mechanically, the game is very impressive for something made in RPG Maker. Excellent sprites and animations and all the art assets are original unlike so many other games made with the engine. Dingaling managed to do so many things with such a limited engine that it's inspiring, really. The game actually manages to take advantage of the limits of the engine in certain ways with things like the bike. Also, the turn-based combat might turn some people off, but there's a lot more to it than most RPG Maker games. For example, with the main character and a few others you can type in combos to do certain skills.
Even more is that Dingaling has said that he's decided to make the planned DLC (The Last Girl) a full fledge game for no charge at all in thanks to the community. He's a cool guy.
One last thing, if you enjoyed Lisa checkout the original game, Lisa The First for some more backstory. It's about an hour or so long and free.

Have you ever wanted to see Mega Man turn into a western?
You know what? Have you ever wished Mega Man was still alive?
This game basically fulfills both of those fantasies. I was actually pretty awestruck at how well this game is designed considering its simplicity. Or maybe that's part of the reason why it works so well. Nothing complex here, just jump'n n shoot'n. It's always a good thing when a platformer explains a gimmick or mechanic without actually having to explain it to you, and boy oh boy there are a lot of those moments in this game.
It has a health system, though I've only played it on Hard because I'm the most harcorest gamer in this plane of existence, that seems to really be more of a heart counter. On hard you get two hits, and being hit once always drops your power up. I assume this changes for the easier difficulties. You get infinite lives, but there's a couple of achievements that encourage you not to die forever. The powerups themselves are different gun types, such as homing shots, spread/tri-shots, rockets, etc, and a traditional western healing item: cake.  Some are found in the level just waiting for you to pick them up, and others seem to be random but frequent-enough enemy drops.
The enemies are typical bad guys in westerners like the guy who likes to shoot at you from windows, the guy who hides behind crates and shoots at you, a DUCK, and mysterious floating sawblades. You know.. Typical westerner villains. OH and there's this train level and the boss is.. well, unexpected considering the enemy types introduced up to that point, but AMAZING NONETHELESS.
The music is nice and varied, but honestly it doesn't sound very spaghetti to me. That being said, it does not detract from the experience at all and I DO like it. It just wasn't as Morricone as I was expecting to be.
Also you're a cowboy/gunslinging damsel/
. This game is the closest you'll ever get to a realistic John Wayne Simulator. I rate it *****/*****.

Short: [9/10] Awesome and challenging Tower Defense x RPG mix with 30+ hours of gameplay. Only a few gripes make this game short of perfect.
Long: "Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten" is a Tower Defense game in which you fight hordes of enemies by using different classes and spells. The classes (of which there are 6) all differ in playstyle and give the game its RPG elements via XP gains, talent trees and weapon/armor aquisition. Even though the game looks simple, it offers a very deep combat and leveling system which will have to be adjusted multiple times in order to beat certain levels. Examples include making your archers target fastest enemies first, putting the stun sword in the hands of your knight, or making sure your ice skills don't get cancelled by your burn ones.  The story itself is amusing as well and gave me a few chuckles along the way. New Game+, 3 star rating per level, and challenges such as endless mode only extend the life of this game and make you want to play more.
There are however, a few issues. Some, like the "Undo" button, which removes ALL the points you just put into your character's skill tree instead of just the last one, should be renamed "Restart" because that's what it actually does. This gets very annoying when respeccing a character with 60 points in New Game+. However, the "Undo" button is not game breaking so it doesn't change my rating of the game. What does, however, is the terrible frame drop encountered during big fights. Even though I have a very powerful rig, it has caused the game to crash several times (once while on 95th wave of endless when attempting 100 wave achievement!). Another is the poor visual of the cursor, which when coupled with the fact the frame rates drop, makes it impossible to see. This has caused me to lose a few games or constantly pause to execute commands.
But the few imperfections get dwarfed by the fact this is a great game, and had me coming back for that "JUST ONE MORE ROUND" feel. The devs are actually pretty cool/active as well and respond quite frequently in the forums. Don't miss this game, it is very much worth it!   [9/10]

At first glance, this is a decent TD.

The story is more engaging than many RPGs and shows great humor.
The achievements are a decent mix of "collect as you go" and "work hard to get this".
The upgrading and customization of your "towers" adds a lot of strategic depth which is only hightened by the weapons and armor you buy/upgrade.
And then you finish the game and find out that there are achievements to play with just the story dependant heroes (Hero Mode). And the challenge increases by a factor of 7.
And then you finish the game doing Hero Mode and find out about New Game +
That's where the game really shines. Because not only is there a whole lot more story, greater challenge in all the previous maps, more achievements AND extra maps... there is also Hero Mode +
And then there are all the bonus maps...
The game is bursting with content, oozing challenge out of every pixel and spurting out humor.
No. Don't wait for a sale. This is not a game you MIGHT want, it is a game you can't NOT have.
PS: There is also a sequel coming. Oh, and a free HD version for everyone who has the game.
These are the kinds of devs you support. Do it.

High Profits. (Get the pun?)
Clicker games are often very much alike. But this is different than all the rest, because it adds a different perspective; Cannabis. As far as i know, as of the date of writing this review, this is the only game on steam that displays cannabis in such a way. Sure, it might be mentioned in a game here, there; but this game actually revolves fully and completely around cannabis, and that is what makes it unique from all the other clicker trash.
The controls are like all the other clicker games. Bottom line, you don't need an instruction manual.
It has some real good 'stoner' stereotypes/puns/cliches to it. I wouldn't expect anything less; not that i dislike it. You have some rather calm stereotypical music playing in the background (only 1 track on repeat), A guy in the background, (presumably you) dressed as a free loving hippy. And well, everything literally is about cannabis.
It has achievements, which is always a nice feature to lure you into playing the game in hopes of getting a 100% rating on the game. For most of the achievements all you have to do is reach a certain currency, except for three that require you to participate in a tournament that you can enter.
It's been strongly accused of being a reskin of Adventure Capitalist. I hadn't played that for quite some time, but i re-installed it to see the similiarities and differences. My finding: Yeah it pretty much is. Same layout, just different names and titles, with High Profits obviously having the puns of weed names and what not. Adventure Capitalist, being around for longer has more features to it though, it has more achievements and it has a more polished look to it.
Yeah, it's a copy of Adventure Capitalist in many ways; but it's good in it's uniqueness of the cannabis. You tell me how much games involve mainstream cannabis. So that's why i recommend it; it is a different type of clicker game to suit a different audience.
So yes it is a reskin of Adventure Capitalist.
When you want, if you want, you can click on a little thing that resembles a cloud. Puff puff it is called (get it?) And this puff puff resets your game; but theres a catch. Doing this is beneficial in getting more profit from your new game after you have reset. You also want to enter Puff Puff when you have a bit of dough saved up in your bank, because that money gets turned into Puff Puff points or whatever, (a special kind of currency) which you can use to get even better upgrades that help in getting more profit.
There are tournaments, but i so far as writing this review, have not entered any. I havn't really seen the point; i think though that it is just another way to increase profits (and three achievements are linked to it.) You of course have to pay currency to enter these tournaments, a high amount of your currency. I'm certain that you don't have to pay gems to enter, but like i've said, i havn't seen the point in entering in the tournament (I also havn't saved up enough money to do so before using Puff Puff.)
The gems are the most valuable piece of currency in the game, and so naturally, you need to pay some real life cash for it. No real point if you ask me. Just wait a couple days for the ingame currency.
And i have read in reviews and comments, that there seems to be a problem with currency transactions or something like that, where people aren't getting what they paid for, if at all.
But paying for gems doesn't interest me, so i'm not going to do it and can't really comment on that in this review.
With a certain high amount of money (i mean high; a decillion. (But did you see what i did there: *High* amount of money?) You can purchase gold bars (1 for every decillion) and these gold bars seem to work the same way as gems do. Gold is another valuable source of currency in the game, just under the gems. It almost, and i say again, almost; is the same as gems, but for some things you still need only gems to do, which seems to be only achievements.
You can also buy Guano (or perhaps more commonly known as manure, but even more commonly known as just $h!t.) This Guano acts how you would expect it to act. It improves your cannabis production and gives you an increase in money.
So there you have it, the review is actually rather longer than i had expected, but never the less, hopefully it will aid you better than just a paragraph. You're reading my review, and so you're reading my opinion. I say it's a good game because as i have stated, it gives you the different perspective of cannabis in a game. That's what makes it unique and a somewhat different game to play.

I'll be honest, to me, this game is fun and I find myself playing over and over again.  Constantly playing as Allies and Germans and trying to find different ways to play.   I'd like to point out some things though that make the game good and ugly.
Pros -
1.  I myself love playing RTS games and I like WW2 Era games, so this game is really fun for me.
2.  The graphics are really pretty and I often catch myself looking at details.
3.  This game does require time management wisely, you have to always make sure to keep things running properly and keep moving your units.
4.  The game does take skill to play and often, noobs need to play against the AI to increase their skill before they get into the "big leagues".
5.  The devs are always making updates to the game and look at other peoples feedback.
6.  You can play other peoples maps and they also pick player maps to be featured on multiplayer.
7.  The game's tutorial helped me (atleast) to understand the game.

8.  The unit variety is pretty wide and there are multiple things each unit can do.
9. There is a wide variety of places to take cover and the maps are pretty beautiful and have very nice designs to them.
10. The gameplay is very smooth and there have been mutliple times where it's either team's game and I can find some really good matches that can last for an hour or two.
Cons -
1.  I hate to say this but, the game is by far a pay to win game.  I myself bought the 2 DLCs that include the extra factions and commanders just to have a fair edge against the ones who bought other OP commanders.
2.  Depending on who you play as or against, the game can be severely unbalanced, a team of Allies who can't get to the Germans quick enough, can't stop their inevebatale armor spam where they constantly spam Panzers, Panthers, or Tigers and not all the AT or tanks in the world could stop it and the Devs have yet to do anything about it.
3.  In my experience, the game is always crashing, even with my new beefed out computer.
4.  I felt that most updates they released, were either really good, or so god awfull that it made the game so unbareable and it made me wanna stop until the next update.
5.  The game gives you only Russia and Germany with just the standard edition and to me, thats definetely, DEFINETELY, not enough for ANY RTS game.
Verdict -
This is my opinion and I get some of you might not like this review but this is my personal experience.

Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

I've been watching this game for a good sale, wanting to play it but a little leery of negative reviews. Finally, it dropped low enough I decided to take the plunge and was actually excited to finally get into the game. And, uh, it's not a good sign when you find yourself asking the player character several times during the opening cutscene to "Stop moving your head. Seriously. STAHP." And that was just the beginning. More cutsences did the exact same thing, and was so bad it distracted from what characters were saying. I kept having to look away thanks to the nausea the camera movement created.
Then there is the actual player movement. Head bob is horrible and can't be disabled. Devs patched out the ability to do so, then apologized and promised a fix, but it still doesn't work. I turned off every other thing I could related to motion sickness triggers, tweaked the game's performance to dramatically raise framerate, and nothing helped. What little time I spent in the game was mostly trying to see if I could "just get used to it" which only made me more and more sick, to the point that I still felt ill hours after giving up.
On the plus side, I put in a refund request to Steam with more detail on the problem, and they did issue me the refund, so thank you Steam support team.
Note to all video game devs: Put head bob and weapon bob on a toggle. Our brains filter that kind of stuff out in real life for a reason.

This is going to be a long passionate review, so if you're not in the mood for that then just take my word that the game is incredible and you should buy it.
A long time ago... in a room not far away from me... I was just a child, with my lovely PS2, who loved Star Wars to death. This day I remember perfectly, it was a cloudy day, me and my dad went to the store to get my long awaited Battlefront 2 game for the PS2. I was so excited for it, and when I got that game box on my hands, the smile from my face never went away as I couldnt stop looking at the cover of the box with the Clone trooper in beetwen Obi Wan and Darth Vader. And to this day, I still have that box saved in my shelf with my other PS2 games. When I got home, I quickly put the disc in my PS2 and the game started running, I heard the wonderful OST of Star Wars in the main menu and I just got so many goosebumps inside of me...but there was only 1 problem... since I got the game from a German shop, the game was in the German language, which I didnt speak much of it, so I didnt really understand much of the dialogue and the main menu options, but I didnt complain, I was grateful and happy for what I had, the language of the game didn't stop me for playing that game day and night, day and night, constantly, even to this day I look back at my younger self and I ask myself, how didnt this game get boring for me? I constantly played the same maps 10 times in a row and then did it with the other maps. The game never stopped being amazing. Eventually though, I got a PC, and I slowly stopped playing on my PS2 and began with PC gaming, but to this day I still remember all the wonderfull times I had with my PS2 and with Star Wars Battlefront 2.
Now almost a decade later, I bought this game for the PC version. And the nostalgia hit me hard, its still such an incredible game to this day and in my opinion, I find this game more enjoyable than EA's new Battlefront games. Now the best part about the PC version of this game, is the ULTIMATE PACK! The Ultimate Pack is a collection of mostly all Star Wars Battlefront 2 mods which bring many new eras, many new units and game modes and much more! And it all works with a simple game launcher which allows you to choose with which mods you'll play it, and there's also this submod you can download which allows you to play multiplayer, its very simple! (You can download the Ultimate Pack on its official website
). The Community of this game really surprised me, I also never knew the community itself made a ''1.3 patch'' which adds new features to the base game and even a free camera mode during battles which lets you take incredible screenshots which I absolutely love.
Star Wars Battlefront 2 is still and in my opinion always will be an incredible game no matter what, and with the Ultimate Pack, it brings endless fun and enjoyment!

The game is also pausable, for those who find some tower defense games too frantic to enjoy.  There are some points where you really need to set the game to slow-mo and pump out the spells you get as their cooldowns time out just to cling to life for another wave, though.

Gunman Clive is a very simple platformer/shooter which takes about an hour to beat. The game has a nice aesthetic to its visuals but the actual gameplay is very weak, with uninteresting levels and enemies making it all feel very trite. There is very little to the game, and the best thing about it is how quickly it can be completed.
Story
Your boyfriend/girlfriend is kidnapped and you must rescue them. It is an excuse plot with no bearing on the game.
Gameplay
The gameplay is very simple and also very poor; there is nothing wrong with the particulars of the controls, though they are sharply limited, but the actual level designs aren’t very interesting and the enemies are all very samey. You run, you shoot, and you jump on platforms, but none of the levels really do anything with it. The shooting powerups are okay, but nothing special – spread shot, a super powerful shot, a penetrating shot, and a tracking shot, none of which are especially exciting.
There are a few different types of enemies, but in the end there is very little to the game itself and the level designs don’t really have anything going for them. The game is very bland and no-frills, and each level takes about a minute to complete – two minutes in the longer levels. As there are only about 16 levels in all, the game is pretty short.
The only real highlight of the game are the four bosses, but even they aren’t very interesting – they are somewhat interesting visually, but gameplay-wise they are the same old attack pattern bosses we all know and love from the games of old, with nothing really to recommend them or make them especially memorable examples of the sort.
Graphics
The game has a nice aesthetic to it, and is pleasing to the eye with its sketchy style.
Final Summary
Gunman Clive is a very cheap game, but the reality is that it still isn’t worthwhile; indeed, it isn’t worth playing for free, because it simply isn’t worth your time. The folks who praised this game gave it very undue praise – they compared it to Megaman, but they left out the fact that he plays like Megaman 1, with far less interesting level design, and far less interesting weapons.

Don't find yourself fooled by the colorful, Earthbound-like graphics and the occasional instances of absurd or witty humor. This game is oppressively dark in more ways than one. It's impossible to say anything about the plot without spoilers: just know that this game is much more "adult" than anything in recent memory. Prepare to feel sorrow, dread, anger, and despair in equal measures. This story will scar your soul in unforeseen ways.
The gameplay unfolds in a typical menu-based, turn-based RPG style, highly reminiscent of that in Earthbound. Luckily, grinding doesn't become necessary if you choose your party well, conserve your scant resources, save frequently, and play smart in battle. Some stark moral choices will arise throughout the game that will make you wish you had more save slots to explore all the options. The soundtrack, as mentioned almost universally by others, excels, and sets a perfectly bleak mood.
If you're craving old-school RPG gameplay laced with a disturbing story and a world dripping with perverse atmosphere (contrasted by the cheerful, retro graphics), you owe it to yourself to try LISA. But, know that it will affect you emotionally, one way or another.
P.S. The controls can be difficult to figure out at first: press F1 at the title screen to reconfigure keybindings. The defaults generally equate to: Enter = select, Esc = cancel, Arrow keys = movement, and WASD = combo keys for battle.

Years later, an unknown cataclysm has rendered the earth near uninhabitable, with all women gone and the world's remaining men dying off

- Can "run" on a potato. The load times are long.

- Can be quite slow. There's a lot to process, especially given the AI's computational needs.
